💡 Key Takeaways
  • West Brom signed Alfie Gilchrist from Chelsea in a deal worth up to £2m in the summer of 2025.
  • It has been revealed that however, a tough debut campaign resulted in Gilchrist dropping down the pecking order.
  • According to recent reports, gilchrist has found the game time he needed in his strongest position, and he’s earned praise for his performances too.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

West Brom signed Alfie Gilchrist from Chelsea in a deal worth up to £2m in the summer of 2025. He enjoyed a positive spell on loan at Sheffield United in the 2024/25 campaign, so there was hope that the promising defender could become a valuable asset for WBA.

It has been revealed that however, a tough debut campaign resulted in Gilchrist dropping down the pecking order. As such, the 22-year-old was sent out on loan to Leyton Orient for the 2026/27 campaign, giving him a chance to play regularly in his preferred role as a centre-back.

According to recent reports, gilchrist has found the game time he needed in his strongest position, and he’s earned praise for his performances too. However, there are some glaring weaknesses that will worry those back at The Hawthorns.

Industry observers note that gilchrist made his first two Leyton Orient appearances off the bench before a spell out through injury. It meant he had to wait until October 10th for his full League One debut, and the West Brom loanee has not relinquished his starting berth since.

According to recent reports, in the last five third-tier games, Gilchrist has helped keep five clean sheets with Orient winning two, losing two and drawing one. He also played the full 90 minutes in the 5-1 FA Cup win over Harborough Town earlier this month.

Industry observers note that with Gilchrist on the pitch, the O’s have conceded 0.53 goals per 90. He has averaged 12.27 defensive contributions per game, along with 9.07 clearances as well.

However, at WBA, there were worries over whether Gilchrist had the physical and aerial presence to deal with powerful Championship forwards. He’s a committed defender, but in terms of winning duels, his struggles have continued out on loan.

Recent findings suggest that gilchrist is averaging a duel success rate of 53.8% with 3.74 won per 90, ranking him in the bottom 18% and 10% of League One centre-backs (all stats via FotMob). The Baggies loanee has shown his ability in one-on-one defending, but when it comes to winning physical battles, he continues to struggle.

From his breakthrough at Chelsea, everyone knows Gilchrist has strong potential as a defender. He’s old-fashioned in the way that he likes to get stuck in and highlights no hesitation in clearing the ball to guard his box.

In a recent development, however, when the game is as physical as it is now, teams need dominance in duels from their centre-backs. Gilchrist could not offer this at West Brom, and it is a weak part of his game at Leyton Orient as well.

It will raise questions over whether Gilchrist can cement a place at centre-back at WBA in the future. Perhaps his defensive ability will see him adapt to a full-back role in time, but if he wants to play at the heart of defence, he seems unlikely to do so in James Morrison’s 4-4-2 setup at Championship level.

Gilchrist will strive to improve in this area though. His mentality and commitment to defending means he can still progress into a fine centre-back, but questions will persist over his chances of doing so at The Hawthorns or in the Championship.

#2569. Tech Report: Inside Boreham Wood, the only unbeaten team in England's top seven tiers: Boss LUKE GARRARD explains how play-off heartache and a 'genius' owner are fuelling his swashbuckling side's promotion bid

Tech Report: Inside Boreham Wood, the only unbeaten team in England's top seven tiers: Boss LUKE GARRARD explains how play-off heartache and a 'genius' owner are fuelling his swashbuckling side's promotion bid

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1433 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 21:00 EST, 12 November 2026 | Updated: 17:17 EST, 13 November 2026.
  • Of 252 clubs in the top seven tiers of English football, the last one unbeaten can be found in the pristine confines of Meadow Park, yards from the studios where the Indiana Jones adventures were filmed.
  • Boreham Wood are on their own crusade.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By MATT BARLOW, FOOTBALL WRITER.

Published: 21:00 EST, 12 November 2026 | Updated: 17:17 EST, 13 November 2026.

Of 252 clubs in the top seven tiers of English football, the last one unbeaten can be found in the pristine confines of Meadow Park, yards from the studios where the Indiana Jones adventures were filmed.

Boreham Wood are on their own crusade. And the Holy Grail is a long-coveted place in the EFL for the runaway leaders of the National League. They have 44 points from 16 games with 44 goals and are 12 points clear ahead of a trip to Yeovil on Saturday, finding success with a distinct passing style.

In a remarkable 4-3 comeback win against Hartlepool earlier this month, Luke Garrard's team made 1,022 passes, beating the Premier League record of 1,015 set by Manchester City against Swansea in April 2018.

The electric start to this campaign is, according to Garrard, fuelled by the lingering pain of defeat in the play-off final at Wembley in May when they conceded an equaliser in the seventh minute of stoppage time and lost on penalties.

'That broke me mentally for four or five days,' the Wood boss tells Daily Mail Sport. 'I reflected hugely and had a long, hard look at myself because I could not walk back for the first day of pre-season without the energy and heart for the job.

'I spoke to the owners and the staff about the first meeting I wanted to have when we came back in. It involved everyone at the club, and it was a message to tell all of them that as much as it hurt us, we needed to use the hurt as our fuel and our driving force.

'We got quite lucky getting some results on the board quite quickly and that builds momentum and belief.'.

National League leaders Boreham Wood, under the guidance of their manager Luke Garrard, are the last unbeaten team in the top seven tiers of English football.

Boreham Wood are a slick operation, skilfully run despite crowds seldom breaking 1,500. They share Meadow Park with Arsenal Women and Arsenal Under 21s and U18s.

According to recent reports, boreham Wood are a slick operation, skilfully run despite crowds seldom breaking 1,500 by chairman Danny Hunter and his son Charlie, who is the sporting director and in charge of recruitment strategy. They are punching above their weight with a mid-table budget.

Hunter senior is a former props master in the film industry who worked at the nearby Elstree Studios among others, and whose father Mickey was a double promotion winning manager of club in the 1970s.

He took control in 1999 and has overseen investment of more than £14million and the rise from the depths of the Isthmian League to the brink of the EFL, forging effective relationships with local authorities and Premier League neighbours Arsenal, who use Meadow Park for their Women, Under-21 and Under-18 teams.

Arsenal ad boards surround an immaculate pitch, and work is underway at the venue on a £4m project to create a covered South Stand terrace incorporating improved 'Fan Zone' style facilities for away fans and a upcoming first-team building.

Garrard's team train in the mornings on the artificial pitches beside the stadium, which are available for community use in the evenings and home in the afternoons to the club's academy.

According to recent reports, manchester City's Iliman Ndiaye and Hull's Sorba Thomas were both nurtured as young players at Boreham Wood. So was Abdul Abdulmalik, a 23-year-old winger signed after his release from Millwall in 2024 and sold to Djurgardens in Sweden for £1.5m in August.

The Abdulmalik fee shattered the non-League record set when Fleetwood Town sold Jamie Vardy to Leicester in 2012.

Industry observers note that there was an untidy episode towards the end of the transfer window when Abdulmalik went public to plead for a move, but the Hunters secured an enviable price for their star and in another example of their good housekeeping have yet to reinvest the money in the team. It is still there as a war chest as they target promotion.

Abdul Abdulmalik, a 23-year-old winger signed after his release from Millwall in 2024, was sold to Djurgardens in Sweden for £1.5million in August.

The club is run by chairman Danny Hunter (pictured) and his son Charlie, who is the sporting director. Hunter Snr is a former props master in the film industry.

The windfall from Wood's famous FA Cup run in 2021-22 was invested into refitting the interiors of the ground including the dressing rooms and swish hospitality areas recognised among the best in non-League.

Meadow Park has a bar bedecked with souvenirs from those games and named in honour of Mark Ricketts, scorer of the goal to beat Bournemouth, who were at the time bound for promotion to the Premier League, and which clinched a date with Everton in the fifth round at Goodison Park.

It has been revealed that 'At no stage has the chairman given me any pressure to generate money from prize funds and cup runs,' says 41-year-old Garrard. 'It's only ever been about creating moments and memories.

In a recent development, 'He (Hunter) is a Boreham Wood boy through and through and it's always been his greatest wish to lead the club into the EFL. He wants to leave a legacy. I adore him, I think he's a genius. We have a great working relationship. I do not take for granted the luxury of being manager here, especially after losing my job two years ago.'.

Garrard has a long association with the club. First as a player, briefly in 2005 and then returning for a second spell four years later, a loan move from Wimbledon which became permanent and led him into his first coaching roles and the manager's job.

He took control in 2015 with the Wood in the top tier of non-League for the first time. Three times they reached the play-offs without promotion and there were many highs including Goodison before Garrard's tearful exit after relegation in April 2024, only for him to be back in charge by September.

During five months away, he turned down interest from one club because it took him too far from his family home and received two direct and sobering rejections from National League clubs. Feedback from the first told him he 'wasn't on the list and never would be' and from the second that he 'wasn't good enough' for them.

In a recent development, perhaps it reveals some of football's inherent petty-mindedness towards Boreham Wood. They are perceived by some as upstarts with limited history and small crowds, putting the noses of 'bigger' clubs out of joint with the streamlined success of their business model and Hunter's backing, like a non-League version of Bournemouth or Brentford.

In a recent development, they have been known to charge scouts for tickets and charge away teams to broadcast, which some refuse to do on a point of principle. For a time, they had a reputation for pragmatic and unattractive football – but not any longer.

Garrard was rejected by two National League clubs and found himself back at Boreham Wood. 'The stars aligned,' as he puts it.

Prolific striker Matt Rush has is fuelling Boreham Wood's promotion push.

In a recent development, garrard was probably entitled to have expected more interest in his services. Instead, he spent two days following the second of those rejections in earnest conversation with his wife about the need to look for work away from football when out of the blue came a call from Boreham Wood.

Recent findings suggest that within another two days he was back in his old job. 'The stars aligned,' as he puts it. 'It was the best team in the National South with the best players, the best facilities and the best budget. I had to go and deliver.'.

And he did. With promotion back to the National League at the first attempt. Then the near-miss heartache of Wembley. Now this early-season surge thanks in part to the goals of striker Matt Rush. The Wood seem to have emerged stronger despite selling their most talented individual, which is a reassuring situation for any coach.

Unbeaten since April in the National League, they scored 25 goals in seven games in October and League One Wigan became the first team to beat them in any competition this season, in the FA Cup first round on Saturday.

It could yet prove a blessing in Boreham Wood's quest for the Holy Grail.

#2560. Breaking: Michael O’Neill makes revelation over Terry Devlin’s Portsmouth future which will leave Championship rivals ‘disappointed’

Breaking: Michael O’Neill makes revelation over Terry Devlin’s Portsmouth future which will leave Championship rivals ‘disappointed’

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (560 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Portsmouth have enjoyed a fine season to date, and versatile star Terry Devlin has been a standout player for John Mousinho’s side.
  • It has been revealed that devlin’s progression has brought interest from elsewhere, but Pompey have been working to secure his future at Fratton Park.
  • “I think he’s in the process of signing a new contract there, and I imagine a lot of teams in the Championship will be disappointed by that.”.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Portsmouth have enjoyed a fine season to date, and versatile star Terry Devlin has been a standout player for John Mousinho’s side. Mainly playing at right-back, the 23-year-old has chipped in with four goals in 14 Championship games, including a brace in the 3-1 win over Swansea City at the start of November.

It has been revealed that devlin’s progression has brought interest from elsewhere, but Pompey have been working to secure his future at Fratton Park. Now, Northern Ireland boss Michael O’Neill has indicated that a positive conclusion is close. Speaking on the player’s situation with BBC Sport over the international break, he mentioned: “He’s a very valuable player for Portsmouth.

“I think he’s in the process of signing a new contract there, and I imagine a lot of teams in the Championship will be disappointed by that.”.

Devlin last extended his contract in February 2025 and he is tied down until 2028. He is in his fourth season with the South Coast outfit, having joined from Glentoran in the summer of 2023.

Tying Devlin down to a new deal marks a key move from Portsmouth. It secures his future before he enters the final 18 months of his current deal, but it also serves as a statement of intent to lock down one of their standout players and most valuable assets.

Industry observers note that the 23-year-old has ups and downs over the course of his Pompey career but as a true utility player, he is a hugely valuable figure in Mousinho’s squad. His athleticism, attitude and well-rounded skillset means he can be trusted to deliver all over the pitch.

Furthermore, the deal will allow Devlin to stay focused on his own game. It will quieten noise over his future and a potential move elsewhere as ambitious sides like Wrexham have previously looked to prise him away from Fratton Park.

At 23, Devlin has time to grow on and off the pitch. On his current trajectory, his value will only grow, so Pompey will be glad to have him tied down to a secure and longer contract.

Sources indicate that as touched on before, Devlin has been the subject of interest from other clubs previously. Those admirers will have been keeping a close eye on his situation with 18 months left on his deal.

However, on a new long-term deal, Portsmouth will be in a better place to stand firm on their valuation. If someone wants to buy him, they will have to pay a handsome fee to do so.

It doesn’t rule out interest or bids, especially if he keeps progressing as he has done, but Devlin’s future at Portsmouth will be far more certain if a newly introduced long-term contract is in place.

#2557. Breaking: Mitochondrial protein import defects enhance tumour immunogenicity

Breaking: Mitochondrial protein import defects enhance tumour immunogenicity

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 27 min read (5489 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~27 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tumour cells evade detection and elimination by the immune system through a suite of adaptations1, including the repression of antigen presentation, which is required for the recognition of tumour cells by CD8+ T cells.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tumour cells evade detection and elimination by the immune system through a suite of adaptations1, including the repression of antigen presentation, which is required for the recognition of tumour cells by CD8+ T cells. Mitochondria have emerged as targets for enhancing antitumour immunity; however, the extensive mitochondrial proteome has remained largely unstudied for its ability to modulate immune responses. Here we show that defects in the mitochondrial protein import machinery promote tumour immunogenicity and synergize with immune checkpoint blockade treatment in melanoma models. Mitochondrial protein import perturbation, specifically through depletion of the TIM23 import complex subunit TIMM50, enhances tumour immunogenicity through a pathway involving mitochondrial DNA escape, cGAS–STING pathway activation and interferon-β (IFNβ) secretion. Secreted IFNβ signals through the type I IFN receptor to activate the JAK–STAT pathway, resulting in increased antigen presentation on MHC class I complexes. Mitochondrial DNA escape in Timm50-depleted cells is linked to the formation of mitochondrial-derived vesicles. Depletion of SNX9 and RAB9, involved in mitochondrial-derived vesicle formation2, suppresses mitochondrial DNA-dependent type I IFN production and signalling. By disrupting mitochondrial proteostasis and membrane architecture, defective protein import in Timm50-depleted cells drives the immune phenotype. This study reveals that mitochondrial protein import inhibition causes tumour immunogenicity, including sensitization to immune checkpoint blockade, by promoting mitochondrial DNA escape and IFNβ-driven MHC class I antigen presentation.

In a recent development, proteomics data have been deposited to the Proteomics Identifications Database (PRIDE) under the accession number PXD069846. RNA-seq data have been deposited to the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) under accession numbers GSE347225 (RNA-seq of YUMM1.7 tumours inoculated in C57BL/6 mice) and GSE320547 (RNA-seq of B16-BL6 and YUMM1.7 cells cultured in vitro). Processed datasets for RNA-seq, proteomics and metabolomics are available as Supplementary Tables. Uncropped blots are provided in Supplementary Fig. 1. For proteomics analysis, the mouse reference proteome (UP000000589) was downloaded from Uniprot in May 2023. The mouse reference genome GRCm39 was used for mapping of RNA-seq reads. Source data are provided with this paper.

Theo Hernandez has been back in Italy during the international break, meeting two of his former colleagues at AC Milan.

Theo first of all got Milan fans talking by posting a photo on his Instagram alongside club legend Paolo Maldini, presumably in Milan. It’s no secret that the French full-back saw the legendary defender as an idol and a role model.

The caption from the Frenchman was simple but telling: “Respect and admiration, always.” In the replies were comments from figures such as Rafael Leao (who wrote ‘I’m coming’) as well as Alessandro Florenzi and Kyle Walker.

A post shared by T H E O H E R N Á N D E Z (@theo3hernandez).

It has been revealed that meanwhile, AllMilan.it (via Goal) are reporting that Zlatan Ibrahimovic met Theo and his family in the city too. Their bond dates back to their years together with the Rossoneri between 2020 and 2022.

Recent findings suggest that they shared the journey to Milan’s 2021-22 Serie A title and forged an important partnership in the dressing room and on the pitch. The defender has described his relationship with the Swede as very close on several occasions.

In a recent development, he has also said more than once that he and his wife Zoe hold the city of Milano close to their hearts. However, for now there are no concrete signs of talks over a possible return to Milan, but rather a chance to meet old friends during the break.

Egypt sack their manager for 'negative impact on team image' after he fainted when fight broke out between his TWO wives with punches and hair-pulling in a bar

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (764 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 13:16 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 13:48 EST, 13 November 2026.
  • Egypt will begin their African Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifying matches with a fresh manager after their previous head coach was sacked amid a torrid breakdown of both of his marriages.
  • Hossam Hassan was handed his marching orders on Saturday after an incident in August which saw his two wives embroiled in a vicious fight, captured and shared on social media.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By TAMARA PRENN, SENIOR SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 13:16 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 13:48 EST, 13 November 2026.

Egypt will begin their African Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifying matches with a fresh manager after their previous head coach was sacked amid a torrid breakdown of both of his marriages.

Hossam Hassan was handed his marching orders on Saturday after an incident in August which saw his two wives embroiled in a vicious fight, captured and shared on social media.

Hassan's first wife Howaida El-Gharbawy and his second Dina 'Dan Adam' Mustafa started the argument while at a hotel bar in the upscale Porto Marina resort on Egypt's north coast.

El-Gharbawy and Mustafa were videoed arguing with Hassan in the middle attempting to cool tensions, but the duo came to blows, with punches thrown and hair pulled as screams filled the air.

Such was the stress of the incident that Hassan is believed to have fainted as he tried to separate the two women.

Horrified public onlookers watched as the physical fight grew with relatives of the trio getting involved, and security was called before Hassan was taken to hospital.

En Égypte, un violent différend a éclaté entre... les deux femmes du sélectionneur égyptien, Hossam Hassan. 🇪🇬😳Le conflit a dégénéré en échauffourée avec coups et tirage de cheveux, avant que des jeunes et des passages n'interviennent dans la bagarre. pic.twitter.com/pvRUSMtAsD.

Egypt head coach Hossam Hassan was sacked this week after a fight broke out between his two wives.

Hassan's first wife Howaida El-Gharbawy and his second Dina 'Dan Adam' Mustafa started the argument while at a hotel in the upscale Porto Marina resort.

The 60-year-old is believed to have fainted while trying to separate the two women.

Both women are believed to have been left with cuts and bruises following the vicious scrap, while Hassan, despite briefly losing consciousness, was left unharmed.

His lawyers later told Sky News Arabia, via the Sun, that he was not suffering a health crisis during the incident, and that he remained in good health.

It has been revealed that but in the days that followed, Hassan started proceedings to divorce El-Gharbawy, who he has been married to for decades. The couple also share three children.

The 60-year-old has a further two children with second wife Mustafa, who Le Parisien alleges also filed for divorce in the days after the footage went viral on social media.

The Egyptian Football Association ensured that Hassan's professional life took a similar nosedive, sharing in a statement that his dismissal was due in part to reputational damage the scandal might be doing to the national team.

'After analysing all the circumstances and events of the past few days, as well as their consequences and the negative impact they have had on the positive image and stability of our national team, the Board of Directors has decided, within the framework of its responsibilities, to dismiss coach Hossam Hassan and his entire technical staff and to end his tenure,' their statement read.

Mustafa's lawyer Mohamed Shams gave an interview on Sky News Arabia claiming that his client had been the victim of a 'premeditated attack'.

'We hoped it wouldn't come to divorce, but things escalated to this level.'.

Hassan married his second wife in 2015, with Egyptian law allowing Muslim men to marry up to four women, providing that any wives have been formally informed that another marriage is to take place.

The law mandates that the husband is also obligated to treat all of his wives equally with regard to housing, financial support and standard of living.

Hassan had been married to his first wife El-Gharbawy for decades, with the pair sharing three of his five children.

Hassan and Mustafa briefly separated four years ago before recoupling before the spat that ended both of his marriages.

As well as being relieved of his duties, Hassan was also sanctioned by the Supreme Council for Media Regulation, leaving him unable to publicly address the media following his sacking.

Mohamed Salah and Co will now play their first qualifier of the international break against Malawi under newly introduced head coach Ali Maher.

The former Liverpool star could be among those Pharaohs stars privately pleased with the departure of Hassan, after he was benched by his ex-manager for the last two international clashes.

When asked why the superstar and national team captain had been left on the sidelines for the ties, Hassan had noted: 'It is not right for a country of 120 million people for the national team to depend on one player.'.

Lionesses take step closer to World Cup but do not look like they can win it

📅 13 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 18 min read (3682 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~18 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • England may have edged a step closer to booking their place at next summer’s Women’s World Cup but they do not yet look like a team who can win it.
  • In a recent development, this two-legged qualifying play-off with Greece was always going to be somewhat academic.
  • The goals flowed more freely in the second half, but Greece deservedly found the net themselves and are not yet out of the tie.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

England may have edged a step closer to booking their place at next summer’s Women’s World Cup but they do not yet look like a team who can win it.

In a recent development, this two-legged qualifying play-off with Greece was always going to be somewhat academic. Greece are ranked 58th in the world and have never qualified for a major tournament. But they could – and should – have taken the lead before England eventually broke the deadlock through Georgia Stanway just before half-time.

The goals flowed more freely in the second half, but Greece deservedly found the net themselves and are not yet out of the tie. There is every chance of the Lionesses winning the second leg in Leicester on Tuesday more comfortably, but not being able to put teams to the sword is exactly why they ended up in the play-offs in the first place.

The best teams are ruthless and unforgiving – and England did not display those traits here. They snatched at chances, and several players were guilty of firing wide. There were also defensive problems. Greece got in behind England’s back line too often and the goal they scored was far too easy for them.

According to recent reports, “I think we made it [the game] a bit harder,” England manager Sarina Wiegman noted. “Greece were very well prepared. They were very well organised and well disciplined. Of course I’m happy with the 3-1, I’m not happy with the one.

In a recent development, “We could have scored more goals, we should have. The final stage, the final pass needs to be better. I think we were a little bit in moments really good on the ball and in other moments not so good, and we could have made better decisions too. Lots of things to take from today.

“Sometimes we played really well, sometimes we were a bit sloppy, so sometimes we were a bit frustrated and I think that’s what you saw.”.

In a recent development, avoid defeat in the second leg and England will play the winners of Ukraine v Slovakia. Ukraine, whom the Lionesses beat 6-1 and 3-0 earlier in their campaign, have a 3-1 lead from their first leg. Perhaps the pedestrian nature of this game was partly because it felt inevitable England would win. They did enough to get over the line but still lacked a clinical edge.

It had been four months since they were thrashed 4-0 by Spain, a defeat which relegated them to the play-offs instead of automatic qualification. They had won every other game in their group before that capitulation, but with Spain topping the group on goal difference, England only had themselves to blame for not scoring more goals in their other fixtures. Breaking down ultra-defensive teams has long been an matter for this Wiegman side and they knew that was what they would be facing in this double-header against Greece.

It did not help that many of Wiegman’s players have been struggling for form in the Women’s Super League this season. Wiegman was also without the ever-reliable Lucy Bronze, who dropped out of the squad on Thursday because of injury. That meant Maya Le Tissier was handed a start at right-back while Laura Blindkilde Brown was preferred to Jess Park in the No 10 position.

It has been revealed that greece were far more open than many would have expected, with several gaps in their defence for England to exploit. They also created problems for themselves by insisting on playing out from the back.

England thought they had taken the lead in style when goalkeeper Fafailia Petaloti gave the ball away needlessly. Lauren James took advantage of Petaloti being off her line and produced a tremendous lob from 25 yards out. But the forward was offside when she picked up the ball and the goal was ruled out by VAR.

Ioanna Papatheodorou nearly gave Greece the lead when she dribbled past Esme Morgan and Leah Williamson with ease but her powerful strike hit the crossbar. It was a let-off for England, but they made it count by taking the lead just before half-time.

A fine team move ended with an excellent Stanway finish. It was her fifth goal in this qualifying campaign and she is England’s top scorer for 2025-26.

She is an exciting player for the future but will feel she has a chance of making a World Cup squad, should England get there. For now, they are taking the slow route.

That’s it for tonight. Let’s hope England can repeat the feat next week.

Stanway is looking to make life difficult for Greece next week, explaining: “We will reflect on that, see where we can minimise them as much as possible, see where we can stop the transition and stop it a little bit earlier and not give them a little bit of a lifeline.”.

Maya le Tissier tells ITV: “I didn’t really know it went in to be honest because I thought the keeper saved it. I just smacked it so I’m very glad. It’s always good to get your first goal, so very happy.

“Not really [a moment she had dreamt about] to be honest because I’m a defender and I thought I’d just be stopping it but it’s always good to get up there. When I play that position, I find myself a little bit higher up, definitely something to work on but very happy to score my first goal.

“I do [like playing that position], I love defending as well. It’s obviously a bit different for me up there but I always try and give my best whatever position I play so I did enjoy it.”.

It has been revealed that she told a pre-match press conference: “It’s just about persistence and trying not to get drawn into being frustrated by the opposition. A really good example was the away game against Ukraine in qualifying. We couldn’t seem to break through in the first half - the keeper was making saves, we hit the woodwork - but the messaging at half-time was just to keep continuing because we were creating opportunities.

Industry observers note that ”Not to start snatching or taking shots from distance, just trusting in our style of play and our ability to find gaps. We came out for the second half and scored really quickly. It’s just about sticking to the strategy and being patient.”.

Erica Meg Parkinson, one of England’s new midfielders, was apparently named after Eric Cantona.

While Cantona still famously is proud of his kung fu kick, when he attacked an obnoxious Crystal Palace fan, Parkison is less enthused by football’s most famous case of breaking the fourth wall.

“My dad is a huge Man United fan so I was named after Eric Cantona,” Parkinson claims. “It’s a pretty good player to be named after except for, you know, the karate kicks.

Sources indicate that “My brother was named after Denis Law. I don’t think my mum had much of a say in the name so she was dragged into it, but it kind of worked out because we both play football now.”.

The excellent Kathryn Batte has run the rule over potential alternatives to Lucy Bronze.

The 35-year-old right-back is out injured, but Ella Toone was called up in her place, rather than a direct replacement.

“Bronze, who is two appearances away from reaching 150 caps for her country, has picked up an injury and returned to Chelsea for treatment,” Batte writes.

“The Lionesses will be missing one of their most reliable players for the matches on Friday and Tuesday, but it gives Sarina Wiegman an opportunity to look at potential replacements for the future.

In a recent development, “Bronze, who has been an integral member of the team throughout Wiegman’s reign, turns 35 later this month. While she will be expected to be the first-choice right-back should England qualify for next year’s World Cup in Brazil, the lack of a recognised back-up has been an ongoing problem.”.

Sarina Wiegman revealed that while dropping Toone was a difficult decision, the midfielder’s reaction left a lasting impression on the coaching staff.

Industry observers note that “When I gave her the call, of course that was a hard call, but she took that straight away,” Wiegman said. “Of course she was very disappointed, but the first thing she did was say: ‘OK, I’m going to get back, I’m going to do that.’”Wiegman was particularly pleased with how Toone handled herself both on the pitch and in front of the media before her late recall.

“That answer in the game, also the way she spoke about it, I thought that was really good,” the head coach added. “And then getting everything ready, I think that really impressed me. Well done, I would say.”.

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Greece vs England in the first leg of the 2027 Women’s World Cup play-offs.

It has been revealed that the Lionesses kick off the two-legged tie tonight looking to secure a solid advantage ahead of Tuesday’s return tie at Leicester’s King Power Stadium. Although they finished level on points with group winners Spain, England’s goal difference sent them into the play-off path, setting up a first-ever senior meeting against a Greek side ranked 55 places below them in the FIFA rankings.

In a recent development, all eyes are on Sarina Wiegman’s selection choices following a turbulent week of squad news. The manager originally raised eyebrows last month by dropping Ella Toone and Chloe Kelly, stating bluntly that “the levels weren’t what I expect from them on the pitch.”.

Toone quickly accepted the setback. Speaking after starting in Manchester United’s victory over Liverpool, the midfielder insisted: “It’s about me now. I’ve got to keep working hard and use it as fuel to come back even better.”.

According to recent reports, that opportunity arrived sooner than expected. An injury sustained by right-back Lucy Bronze - described by Wiegman as “really small” - forced the defender to return to Chelsea for assessment. Wiegman immediately turned to Toone, who flew directly to Greece from Spain, where she had been running her own self-directed training block during the international window.

With 69 caps and 24 international goals to her name - including crucial strikes in the Euro 2022 final and the 2023 World Cup semi-final - Toone brings proven substantial-match experience back into the setup at a critical moment.

We will bring you all the build-up, confirmed team news, and live play-by-play coverage throughout the evening.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that QPR have made a fine start to this season and currently occupy the final Championship play-off spot.
  • In a recent development, scarlett joined the club from Arsenal in April 2025, and so far this season he has made six appearances and clubs are starting to notice.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that QPR have made a fine start to this season and currently occupy the final Championship play-off spot. The likes of Pierce Charles and Ronnie Edwards have earned the plaudits, while Richard Kone is finding his form again in attack, but a real breakout star has been 17-year-old Leon Scarlett.

In a recent development, scarlett joined the club from Arsenal in April 2025, and so far this season he has made six appearances and clubs are starting to notice. Anthony Joseph has noted that European giant AC Milan are tracking his progress after his start to the campaign.

The Italian side are not the only side keen, with Eintracht Frankfurt also keeping tabs on Scarlett’s situation. Both sides have expressed interest in the winger, who is already a Wales under-21 international.

QPR youngster Scarlett is attracting growing attention after breaking into Julien Stephan’s first-team prepares this season, with AC Milan and Eintracht Frankfurt reportedly monitoring his progress.

The 17-year-old Welsh winger joined QPR in January 2025 after spending around a decade in Arsenal’s academy, having been released by the Gunners. Primarily operating on the left, Scarlett is known for his explosive acceleration, close control and ability to beat defenders in one-on-one situations.

In a recent development, he made his senior debut aged 16 in May 2026 and has featured regularly from the bench, but he did start against Preston back in September, accumulating around 130 minutes. He has also represented Wales at multiple youth levels, including the U21s.

Manager Stephan has praised his personality and willingness to express himself in first-team training, with QPR viewing him as an exciting prospect. He is playing ahead of his age right now and QPR fans have every right to be excited about Scarlett’s potential.

QPR must resist interest from AC Milan and Eintracht Frankfurt in Scarlett, with the 17-year-old better off continuing his development at Loftus Road.

Recent findings suggest that scarlett has enjoyed a rapid rise since leaving Arsenal’s academy, earning first-team opportunities under Stephan. However, with only around 130 Championship minutes to his name and no senior goal or assist yet, a move abroad would arguably come too soon.

Stephan has a proven record of developing young talent, while QPR are placing increasing emphasis on their academy pathway. Scarlett’s explosive pace, close control and ability to beat defenders make him an exciting prospect, but he needs regular exposure to senior football to refine his game.

A move to Milan or Frankfurt could leave him fighting for opportunities in youth sides rather than progressing at first-team level. QPR should keep hold of Scarlett, gradually increase his involvement and allow his performances and value to grow before considering a substantial-money departure.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • AC Milan are in the market for a fresh central defender ahead of the winter window, and three names are on the list.
  • According to La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below), Gerry Cardinale wants to give Ruben Amorim at least two signings in January.
  • Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AC Milan are in the market for a fresh central defender ahead of the winter window, and three names are on the list.

According to La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below), Gerry Cardinale wants to give Ruben Amorim at least two signings in January. One of them will be a centre-forward – with Nicolo Tresoldi the ambitious idea at the moment – while the other will be a defender.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

With Matteo Gabbia sidelined until well into January and Fikayo Tomori at the moment injured, Amorim has been juggling an emergency in recent weeks. It was a situation further compounded by an issue that arose for Strahinja Pavlović last week.

Fortunately for Amorim, he has found a capable alternative in the youngster Sankhoun Diawara. Looking ahead, however, the club is considering an addition that could immediately boost the level of the department.

It has been revealed that A summer target was Gonçalo Inácio whom Amorim knows well, having coached him for years at Sporting CP. Dialogue with the Lisbon club has continued even during the current period when the transfer window is closed, following the failure to reach an agreement before.

Milan could renew their pursuit soon, though there is at the moment no consensus regarding his asking price. Furthermore, Inácio is left-footed and has primarily played as an outside centre-back throughout his career.

Sources indicate that what the Rossoneri need right now is more of a right-footed player capable of rotating between a wide centre-back role and a central position. While it is true that Gonçalo adapted to the right side under Amorim, there are other candidates who are a more natural fit for that role.

For instance, Ismaelo Ganiou of RC Lens has been on the radar for some time. His contract renewal in August does not necessarily rule out a transfer, although there has been no further contact with the French club since initial discussions in the summer.

Among the upcoming names, 21-year-old Massiré Sylla of Union Saint-Gilloise is an intriguing prospect. The Belgian club have also moved rapidly to secure their young star with a new contract until 2031. That mentioned, it is not a major obstacle, and the price is around €15m.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • AC Milan still retain an interest in signing Juan Miranda after being linked with him in previous years, a report claims.
  • Tuttosport write this morning that Miranda is establishing himself as one of the best specialists in his position in Europe.
  • No one in Serie A has more than that, and his creativity was seen first hand in Bologna’s comeback win at San Siro.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AC Milan still retain an interest in signing Juan Miranda after being linked with him in previous years, a report claims.

Tuttosport write this morning that Miranda is establishing himself as one of the best specialists in his position in Europe. The numbers speak for themselves: he’s already provided six assists in the first part of the season.

No one in Serie A has more than that, and his creativity was seen first hand in Bologna’s comeback win at San Siro. Naturally, his performances have not gone unnoticed in Italy and England. The first inquiries are beginning to arrive, with a contract situation that is worth keeping an eye on.

Recent findings suggest that the paper writes that Miranda is also appreciated by Milan, although the Rossoneri are kicking themselves a bit too. They had an agreement to sign him on a free transfer two years ago and then decided to walk away. In hindsight, it looks like a major mistake.

Bologna seized the transfer opportunity in the summer of 2024, and are now enjoying his exploits. At the same time, however, concern is beginning to mount given that his deal with the Rossoblu expires in just 19 months.

This is why the Bologna management have been trying to establish talks regarding a contract extension in the past few weeks. The work so far hasn’t led to great progress, and so the possibility of a sale to avoid losing the Spaniard in a cut-price deal (or even for free) may be evaluated.

Juventus are in the running too, and an immediate attempt to bring him to Continassa and give Luciano Spalletti the left-back he’s coveted since last summer can’t be ruled out. This is especially true if the Bianconeri are in contention for a top-four finish.

In a recent development, beware of the Palladino effect: since the coach took over at Bologna, the Rossoblu have been soaring (17 points in seven games). If the Emilian side were to also be involved in the fight for a European spot, it would be more difficult to pry Miranda from them.

League One clubs target Linfield winger amid impressive form

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (513 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Rhys Brennan’s form has attracted the attention of League One sides, who face competition from teams in the SPL.
  • According to recent reports, brennan, 20, is predominantly a right winger.
  • Bohemian right now sit 3nd in the Irish Premier Division, whilst Linfield top the Northern Irish Premiership, having won 12 of their 16 matches so far.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rhys Brennan’s form has attracted the attention of League One sides, who face competition from teams in the SPL. At this moment in time, none of the admirers are named in O’Rourke’s report.

According to recent reports, brennan, 20, is predominantly a right winger. He is out on loan with Linfield away from Bohemian, where his contract runs out next December.

Bohemian right now sit 3nd in the Irish Premier Division, whilst Linfield top the Northern Irish Premiership, having won 12 of their 16 matches so far. Brennan has contributed well to their success, locking down a starting berth on the flanks.

Brennan broke into the Bohemian side in 2025 and has since developed on loan at Cobh Ramblers before Linfield. A move to England would constitute a major step in Rhys Brennan’s career, should it take place.

According to recent reports, brennan’s debut for Bohemian came against Waterford at the end of the 2024 campaign. He soon followed that up with a first goal the following Monday, scoring as his side overturned a 2-0 deficit to win 3-2 against Shamrock Rovers.

Sources indicate that brennan has also featured for the Republic of Ireland U19s. The winger made his debut for the side away against Slovakia in a 3-1 friendly victory back in March 2024.

According to recent reports, the young winger is an energetic presence on the wing. He’s shown he can offer a dual threat of goals and assists, but his crossing ability and work rate is where he stands out.

According to recent reports, furthermore, Brennan is a confident presence on the wing. He leads the way for Linfield with regard to successful dribbles per match this season, averaging 1.9 successful dribbles per 90.

Recent findings suggest that this season is the first season where Brennan is fully flourishing in senior football. Should he make the move to England, he might need time to adapt given the step up from Northern Ireland to League One.

Brennan will not walk into a side challenging for promotion and integrate himself with regular minutes. Equally, a relegation battle would not be beneficial for his career.

A move to a mid-table side seems safe, giving Brennan a low pressure environment to develop and express himself on the wings.

In a recent development, linfield will be reluctant to lose Rhys Brennan this season. However, should the player’s form continue, he may be a serious candidate for a move in the January transfer window, and a decision will ultimately be made by his parent club Bohemian.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that A fresh epoch for direct visualization of accretion dynamics near the event horizon of a black hole began when the Event Horizon Telescope Collaboration synthesized an Earth-sized aperture with millimetre radio interferometry and published the first reconstructed image1,2,3,4 of a black hole shadow at the core of radio galaxy Messier 87 (M87). The image appeared as a ring-like structure, representing the gravitationally lensed and redshifted emission around the central supermassive black hole, M87*, located at the galactic nucleus. However, application of various data analysis and imaging heuristics resulted in divergent representations of M87* fine-scale features3,5,6,7, with some external analyses even challenging the fundamental ring-like morphology of the source8,9. Such difficulties arise as a consequence of the inherent sparsity of the very long baseline interferometry measurements, making interferometric image reconstruction an inadequately constrained problem. Moreover, the solution is sensitive to instrument calibration, post-processing algorithms and imaging hyperparameters. Here we apply an independent imaging algorithm that we have developed to the M87* dataset that is free from prescriptive morphological priors and founded on observables immune to instrument calibration errors. We reconstruct the black hole shadow image and unequivocally reproduce a ring-like morphology, with an angular diameter of 42.2 ± 1.5 μas corresponding to a black hole mass of 6.5 ± 0.5 billion solar masses assuming nominal scaling parameters, observed at an inclination angle of approximately 20° from the approaching jet.

The M87* supermassive black hole, with a mass of MBH = (3–7) × 109 M⊙ (refs. 10,11,12) located at a distance of D = 16.8 Mpc (refs. 13,14), offers a unique window into horizon-scale general relativistic physics. Its appearance on event horizon scales is expected, on the basis of general relativistic predictions, to be dominated by a central shadow, which, for a non-rotating Schwarzschild black hole, is characterized by a critical impact parameter that is proportional to the black hole mass15 as \(3\sqrt{3}G{M}_{{\rm{BH}}}/({c}^{2}D)\), in which G is the gravitational constant and c is the speed of light. To observe with a spatial resolution capable of detailing the M87* black hole shadow requires unprecedented μas-scale angular resolution, roughly equivalent to the angle subtended by the width of a strand of human hair more than 1,000 km away. Achieving this feat requires a combination of millimetre wavelengths (λ ≈ 1 mm) and an effective aperture size comparable with the diameter of the Earth.

Sources indicate that such a synthesis of an Earth-sized aperture was realized through very long baseline interferometry (VLBI) techniques by correlating the signals from a global network of independent radio observatories, collectively referred to as the Event Horizon Telescope (EHT)1,16. As the Earth rotates, the separation vectors between pairs of geographical stations sweep out elliptical arcs that incrementally fill the Earth-sized synthetic aperture. Although this technique yields the requisite angular resolution to image the M87* shadow, the resulting virtual aperture remains substantially unfilled and lacks the sensitivity and reconstruction fidelity of a filled aperture. The data sparsity problem is further compounded by the requirement of calibrating rapid, station-based atmospheric phase and amplitude fluctuations on continental-scale separations, which often occur on timescales shorter than the coherence time of the observations.

Industry observers note that these inherent challenges make image reconstruction from VLBI and EHT datasets an ill-posed problem, highly sensitive to instrument calibration and post-processing heuristics. Present algorithms regularly use manually tuned and independently weighted data terms and regularizations to bias the solution towards plausible morphologies, which can inadvertently steer the reconstruction towards preferred solutions. The consequences are divergent representations of the fine-scale features of M87*, such as the surface brightness distribution and hotspot localization3,5,6,7,17,18. Using traditional approaches, including CLEAN-based algorithms or hybrid mapping with self-calibration19,20,21,22,23, independent analyses showed that the resulting reconstruction is sensitive to methodological and hyperparameter selections, such as image initialization6 or adopted field of view8, with some independent analyses demonstrating reconstructions without a clear ring-like structure8,9, suggesting that, if the field of view extends to circular diameters beyond 120 μas, a single elongated bright spot solution is favoured over a ring8.

It has been revealed that to resolve the tension around the M87* results and advance beyond methodological uncertainties, we transition from traditional approaches towards a more autonomous and objective framework. The independence of our method is primarily grounded on our use of robust interferometric observables, called closure invariants24,25,26,27, which capture information on source morphology that is unaffected by errors in wavefront and instrument calibration. Therefore, closure invariants constitute robust information-bearing observables in radio interferometry, underpinning high-fidelity morphology reconstructions28,29,30,31. Closure invariants are also insensitive to absolute position and absolute flux scale, but these are not inherent morphological parameters. In contrast to the disparate closure phases24 and closure amplitudes25 that have traditionally served as such robust observables, the closure invariants formalism26,27 that we use provides a unified framework that carries equivalent information while eliminating the requirement for heterogeneous treatment typically observed in the literature. By making use of the rich calibration-independent, pure morphological information carried by closure invariants, we can bypass conventional techniques that require sensitive calibration tuning and observer-driven priors.

Recent findings suggest that to take full advantage of the closure formalism, we develop and apply the Generative Deep learning Image Reconstruction with Closure Terms (GenDIReCT)31 algorithm, trained on images unrelated to astronomy and designed to generatively produce data-driven image reconstructions using only closure invariants. Unlike other machine-learning-based radio interferometric imaging algorithms, our algorithm is unique in using closure invariants to condition a latent diffusion model. GenDIReCT has undergone extensive testing on both synthetic31 and real data32 and has been demonstrated to be capable of consistently recovering diverse morphological structures, without manual intervention, prescriptive priors or parameter tuning (further detail in Methods).

For the first time, to our knowledge, closure invariants are used to image M87* through our GenDIReCT algorithm, using the publicly available 1.3-mm EHT measurements from four observation epochs (5 April, 6 April, 10 April and 11 April) from 2017 (ref. 1), two epochs (21 April and 25 April) from 2018 (ref. 33) and two epochs (13 April and 18 April) from 2021 (ref. 34). We set several fields of view for the reconstruction (128 × 128, 225 × 225 and 450 × 450 μas2), in which each combination of dataset and field of view is an independent model and acts as an indirect prior on the maximum source size. For each of these models, we aggregate a large population of generative reconstructions into a single representative median image, comparing them with the Event Horizon Telescope Collaboration (EHTC) fiducial reconstruction that is reproduced using the public eht-imaging pipeline (https://github.com/eventhorizontelescope/2019-D01-02). We also derive a composite image from the pixelwise median of all reconstructions of each epoch across all fields of view aligned to the single reconstruction with the best data fidelity score.

In a recent development, all datasets from independent observation epochs convincingly produce a compact, ring-like structure on an approximately 40-μas scale. On the highest-quality dataset of each year (11 April 2017, 21 April 2018 and 18 April 2021), our median reconstruction is a compact circularized ring of consistent orientation and diameter, independent of the reconstruction field-of-view window and brightened in the south or southwest direction. The appearance of the ring is most consistent with an observed inclination angle of about 20° from the approaching jet. We present the composites for our best reconstructions from these three datasets in Fig. 1.

It has been revealed that the dashed ellipses represent the full width at half maxima of the synthesized point spread functions. The bottom row illustrates the composite reconstructions convolved with a 20-μas circular beam, comparable with fiducial EHTC image reconstructions of M87*. Image reconstructions in the top row are unconvolved. Here intensity is illustrated in a normalized linear scale, in which the compact flux density of M87* is constrained by other means to be between 0.4 Jy and 1.0 Jy (refs. 3,33,34).

Sources indicate that the consistency of the source size (about 40 μas) across all fields of view is strong confirmation of a compact source. Under the most-constrained 128 × 128-μas2 field of view, the median reconstructed image exhibits the highest image-domain similarity score with fiducial EHTC reconstructions and the performance on data adherence metrics is competitive with those of larger fields of view, supporting the prior expectation that extended emission of the M87* jet is unconstrained by the EHT datasets3,33. On some infrequent reconstructions of epochs with lower-quality datasets suffering from even sparser aperture coverage3, lower signal-to-noise ratio or various observation deficiencies33, the ring-like morphology can become less clear, as noted by independent studies8. Consequently, the suggested sensitivity of image morphology to the assumed field of view reported in independent reanalyses and demonstrated for the 5 April 2017 dataset8 is possibly an artefact of insufficient aperture coverage or low-quality data. In our work, when higher-quality datasets are considered, the sensitivity to field of view disappears, contrary to predictions based on the traditional hybrid mapping approach8. Our work thus yields a robust, independent verification of the ring-like geometry characteristic of the M87* black hole shadow image.

In a recent development, in contrast to regularized maximum likelihood methods in the publicly available imaging pipelines used by the EHTC on M87*, our method does not require manually prescribing an image initialization. For instance, the eht-imaging pipeline applied on M87* is initialized with a 40-μas full width at half maximum (FWHM) Gaussian, which serves as a powerful prior on the characteristic source size. These methods typically exhibit marked sensitivity to the starting model6. When the eht-imaging pipeline is initialized with Gaussian priors larger than 40 μas (that is, 80–120 μas), the resulting image reconstructions exhibit phantom repetition or aliasing artefacts, which is a common concern for VLBI imaging algorithms28,35.

It is notable, therefore, that we consistently recover a single, compact source morphology in the absence of manual prescriptions. When our model is trained on different fields of view, the model learns an implicit statistical prior from its diverse training library conditioned on the input interferometric observables, namely, closure invariants. The convergence towards a stable, singular ring structure across varying fields of view indicates that the our model is successfully inferring the intrinsic source geometry from the data itself, rather than operating within the constraints of a manually selected initialization. The autonomy and capacity for imaging directly from calibration-independent observables of GenDIReCT represents a notable step towards objective blind imaging in the challenging data-sparse VLBI regime. By unequivocally recovering the ring-like structure of M87* across several datasets through this approach, we provide a rigorous cross-validation of published EHTC results.

Recent findings suggest that we quantitatively demonstrate consistency with the EHTC image reconstructions by measuring ring characteristics from our reconstructed images and comparing them with published parameters. We apply an independent implementation of the image-domain feature extraction method used by the EHTC3 to measure ring properties from reconstructed event-horizon-scale images, including ring diameter, width, orientation (measured anticlockwise from north), azimuthal asymmetry and central brightness fraction. The measured properties from our median reconstructions of all datasets are presented in Table 1. Each cell represents the mean parameter measured from independent reconstructions on all three fields of view.

The measured ring orientation and diameter remain relatively stable between the GenDIReCT and EHTC imaging methods. In Fig. 2, we compare our image-domain measurements derived from our reconstructions with the EHTC analogue. There is a clear anticlockwise trend in the ring orientation angle as measured by all methods between the 5 and 6 April reconstructions with 10 and 11 April in 2017, as well as between the 2017 and 2018/2021 observations. However, the evolution in 2017 may be caused by uncertainty in the azimuthal structure brought about by the sparse aperture coverage of observations taken on 5 and 6 April. Nevertheless, the evolution in ring orientation between the 2017 and 2018 observations is noteworthy, attributable to the turbulent nature of black hole accretion36. In particular, the observed ring orientation in 2018 and 2021 are closer in alignment with the large-scale forward jet of M87* compared with that in 2017.

Comparison of ring diameter and orientation measured from image-domain feature extraction applied on our reconstructions with values from the EHTC, separated by observation epoch. EHTC measurements on each epoch correspond to different imaging algorithms (from left to right: THEMIS, DIFMAP, eht-imaging, SMILI and Comrade). Our measurements are presented with two estimates of uncertainty: the dashed line delineates the dispersion (along the azimuthal axis for diameter and along the radial axis for orientation) in the image-domain feature extraction method and the solid line with triad cap indicates the standard deviation across fields of view, which is unique to our method. For the diameter, we illustrate the mean and 1σ standard deviation for EHTC methods and our method with the dashed line and sheath. The highest-quality dataset of each year is highlighted in yellow.

Recent findings suggest that conversely, the measured ring width and central brightness fraction are heavily influenced by methodological differences, as seen in the variation between imaging algorithms. For instance, reconstructions from the DIFMAP algorithm37 are convolved with a 20-μas circular beam, which inflates the ring width compared with regularized maximum likelihood methods and our algorithm. Likewise, the azimuthal asymmetry parameter is unstable between different days and different methods, which is indicative of sensitivity to variation in the aperture coverage. Therefore, the ring width and central brightness fraction probably do not reflect intrinsic source properties.

Sources indicate that to further cross-validate the measured ring parameters, we use a complementary Bayesian forward-modelling framework to fit the observed closure invariants using a superposition of primitive geometric shapes with analytic visibilities. With the ring-like structure firmly established by our independent, calibration-insensitive and non-parametric imaging algorithm, we proceed to construct our geometric composite using the xsringauss4 model as a foundation. We include one centralized large Gaussian and two elliptical nuisance Gaussians with independent spatial offsets to help capture non-ring short-spacing flux and extraneous emission. Using the DYNESTY nested sampling algorithm38, we perform parameter estimation for the xsringauss model for each epoch. Figure 3 demonstrates the posterior covariance from geometric modelling of the 11 April 2017 and 21 April 2018 datasets, in which the one-dimensional and two-dimensional marginalized posterior distributions of the outer radius, inner radius, eccentricity, fading parameter and orientation are illustrated. We apply the image-domain feature extraction method on the geometric image model derived from the median value of each one-dimensional posterior distribution to measure all characteristic ring parameters. Posterior covariances for all other datasets are provided in Methods. In all epochs, we measure a mean diameter and standard deviation of d = 42.3 ± 1.1 μas from forward geometric modelling of closure invariants, which is compatible with the mean d = 42.2 ± 1.5 μas from our non-parametric image reconstructions.

According to recent reports, a, The one-dimensional and two-dimensional marginalized posterior distributions and median values for the outer radius, inner radius, eccentricity, fading parameter and orientation. b, The composite images created from all GenDIReCT reconstructions across all fields of view are presented in comparison with the fitted median xsringauss sky models. The diameter is measured with image-domain feature extraction and the corresponding uncertainty is from azimuthal dispersion rather than the sample variance across several fields of view.

Inferring the gravitational radius of the black hole, and hence its mass, from the measured ring diameter requires independently calibrating the imaging method with synthetic data from simulated models of lensed black hole accretion emission4. The prior expectation for the mass of the central black hole in M87 is primarily sourced from high-quality gas12 and stellar11 dynamical estimates, which measured \({M}_{{\rm{gas}}}=3.{5}_{-0.7}^{+0.9}\times 1{0}^{9}{M}_{\odot }\) and Mstar = (6.6 ± 0.4) × 109 M⊙, respectively. Using our measured ring diameter, distance measure of \(16.{8}_{-0.7}^{+0.8}\,{\rm{Mpc}}\) and nominal scaling parameters for the gravitational radius, we estimate a black hole mass of MBH = (6.5 ± 0.5) × 109 M⊙ for M87*.

Sources indicate that our independently measured ring diameters and inferred black hole mass from GenDIReCT imaging and geometric modelling are therefore in excellent agreement with previous stellar dynamical mass measurements11 and with image-domain feature extraction on the imaging methods applied by the EHTC. By contrast, the smaller ring diameter predicted by the black hole mass estimate from gas dynamics would have been challenging to resolve given the EHT beam dimensions of approximately 20 μas. Future observations with the James Webb Space Telescope Near-Infrared Spectrograph integral field unit will provide further detail on the kinematics within the central arcsecond of the M87 core39, producing finer constraints on the M87* black hole mass.

In a recent development, the appearance of the black hole shadow is also sensitive to the black hole spin, a⁎, and observed inclination angle. We compare our composite M87* reconstructions with synthetic 230-GHz images of M87* produced by the IPOLE algorithm40, which integrates the covariant radiative transfer equation over relativistic photon trajectories across fluid data from general relativistic magnetohydrodynamic (GRMHD) simulations41. Quantitative analysis using the normalized cross-correlation similarity score, ρNX, comparing beam-convolved synthetic images with image reconstructions, identifies a clear sensitivity to inclination. We present the results based on composites from highest-quality datasets for all years in Fig. 4. Note that we do not explore inclination angles >90°, as the resulting synthetic images are comparable with an inversion of the spin direction. Although the highest similarity scores favour a non-zero black hole spin, our analysis does not constrain the spin magnitude, consistent with previous analyses with EHT36 and non-EHT data42. Altogether, the best-scoring inclination is approximately 20° and, although the best-scoring inclination in the a⁎ = 0 case is much higher, such models are disfavoured a priori by independent considerations of jet power43,44,45 and precession42. Consequently, the results from our image-domain comparative analysis are generally consistent with the fiducial 17.2° ± 3.3° jet viewing angle inferred from 43-GHz VLBI observations46,47. Future horizon-scale imaging with space-based VLBI offers the potential to resolve the M87* photon ring48, which would enable a direct and precise determination of the black hole spin, at present unconstrained by an image-domain analysis.
