This work uses the publicly available network-calibrated datasets of M87* (https://eventhorizontelescope.org/for-astronomers/data), reduced through the EHT-HOPS pipeline, on the basis of observations obtained in 2017 (ref. 2), 2018 (ref. 33) and 2021 (ref. 34). In 2017, EHT observations of M87* were conducted with seven separate facilities1: the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA)49,50, the Atacama Pathfinder Experiment telescope (APEX)51, the Large Millimeter Telescope (LMT)52, the Pico Veleta IRAM 30-m telescope (PV)53, the Submillimeter Telescope Observatory (SMT)54, the James Clerk Maxwell Telescope (JCMT)55 and the Submillimeter Array (SMA)56, which heterogeneously and sparsely sample the Fourier plane as the Earth rotates. Furthermore, the Greenland Telescope (GLT)57,58 participated in the 2018 observations for the first time as part of the EHT array, which improved the aperture coverage, particularly along the north–south direction. For 2021, the 12-m Kitt Peak (KP)59 telescope and the upgraded Northern Extended Millimeter Array (NOEMA)60 facility joined EHT observations for the first time.

According to recent reports, the 2017 observations of M87* are spread over four separate epochs (5, 6, 10 and 11 April), whereas observations in 2018 and 2021 are separated into two epochs each (21/25 April for 2018 and 13/18 April for 2021). The datasets with the best single-day aperture coverage each year are 11 April, 21 April and 18 April, which we use as our fiducial datasets, whereas datasets on other days are used as cross-validation. We consider the data taken over two approximately 2-GHz bands centred at 227.1 (low) and 229.1 GHz (high), which we merge into a single dataset.

Recent findings suggest that the interferometric data on M87* comprise complex visibilities, correlated from signals between pairs of stations, referred to as a baseline, which are, by the van Cittert–Zernike theorem61, related to the source brightness distribution by a two-dimensional Fourier transform after certain approximations62. Visibilities can be sequenced into scans, on the basis of the time difference between observations, from which we obtain coherently averaged visibilities. In this work, closure invariants are generally computed from scan-averaged visibilities. With typical scan lengths on the order of five minutes, temporal averaging can potentially introduce residuals from time-dependent gain fluctuations to closure invariants. We have internally validated the robustness of our imaging products by computing closure invariants at the smallest possible cadence of the science-ready dataset (typically 10 s) before scan-level averaging. Following the procedure in the publicly available M87* imaging pipeline (https://github.com/eventhorizontelescope/2019-D01-02), we rescale short baselines to the total flux density estimated from the ALMA and APEX baseline to excise the contribution from extended flux. We have also internally validated that the short baseline rescaling procedure does not affect the recovered morphology from our imaging algorithm. For quantitative comparison, we generate fiducial images from the publicly available eht-imaging pipeline to represent EHTC reconstructions.

In a recent development, closure invariants are calibration-independent interferometric measurables produced from a generalized formalism of traditional closure phase24,63 and amplitudes25, with both a co-polar version26 and a polarimetric version27. GenDIReCT uses co-polar closure invariants constructed from elementary triangular plaquette variables called ‘advariants’. The complete minimal set of independent closed triads can be constructed from an array of n stations by selecting all pairs of array elements (a, b) pinned on a fixed reference vertex indexed at 0,.

It has been revealed that in which \({{\mathcal{V}}}_{{ab}}^{{\prime} }\) are corrupted visibilities measured from the baseline between stations a and b and |g0|2 is the unknown scaling factor associated with the reference station, which is shared by all complex advariants constructed in this way. By normalizing all advariants by the L2-norm, for example, we produce \({N}_{{\rm{s}}}^{2}-3{N}_{{\rm{s}}}+1\) real-valued independent closure invariants, whose form is different but carry information equivalent to that in traditional closure amplitudes and phases. In the co-polar formalism of closure invariants, traditional closure phases can be identified trivially from the phases of the advariants, whereas closure amplitudes can be derived from specific pairs of advariants. A key advantage of this formalism over traditional closure amplitudes and phases is that it avoids the heterogeneous treatment that phases and amplitudes necessitate. In internal validation tests, closure invariants as the sole likelihood term was found to be preferable over the independently weighted (log-)closure amplitudes and closure phases in terms of convergence and data efficiency.

According to recent reports, various selections of the reference station can affect covariances between closure terms, despite carrying equivalent information. A different selection of reference station can influence the signal-to-noise ratio in the derived closure invariants but does not greatly influence the resulting image reconstruction32. For this work, to avoid bias from a single reference station selection, we present the combined results from two GenDIReCT models for each dataset, trained consistently on the first and the second most sensitive stations as the reference stations in each scan. Selecting from among the most sensitive stations maximizes closure-invariant signal-to-noise ratio and minimizes covariances between closure terms64.

The GenDIReCT31 algorithm is an imaging algorithm that uses co-polar closure invariants26 for calibration-independent imaging under the constraints of sparse aperture coverage characteristic of VLBI data. The architecture comprises a latent diffusion model65 conditioned on closure invariants and a multilayer convolutional neural network (CNN) used to optimize the closure invariants likelihood. Traditional imaging algorithms, such as hybrid mapping and self-calibration followed by deconvolution, begin with a simple initial model and iteratively solve for antenna-based complex gains and the image model to converge on a final solution that matches the measured data. These methods can be sensitive to and biased by image initialization and calibration errors, particularly in sparse and low signal-to-noise measurements6,19,22. Our algorithm bypasses the limitations of conventional techniques by using closure invariants as the robust interferometric measurable and produces an image reconstruction directly in a single forward pass. Furthermore, in contrast to the newer regularized maximum likelihood methods that can also image using closure invariants as the sole data term28,35,66,67, our algorithm provides a generative solution that does not require a user-specified, hand-tuned image initialization at inference time. Other machine learning interferometric imaging techniques have been presented in the literature, on the basis of CNNs68,69,70,71,72, normalizing flow73,74, denoising diffusion74,75, classifiers29,76, adversarial networks76,77 and transformers30. Although there are some similarities with other diffusion-based imaging algorithms74,75, GenDIReCT is unique in its closure-conditioned latent diffusion model and, notably, in its use of homogeneous closure invariants rather than the traditional closure phases and closure amplitudes that require heterogeneous treatment. In this section, we provide a brief overview of our algorithm and its past applications.

The neural network architecture is composed of two distinct components. The first component is a conditional U-Net78 based on textually conditioned image generation architectures65 with denoising diffusion probabilistic models79, which has emerged as a highly effective image generation technique, capable of modelling complex data distributions. Our implementation is a latent diffusion model consisting of three convolutional layers set in a symmetric contracting and expanding pathway with residual connections80 from the contracting path that map features to their mirrored expanding layers. In the contracting path, we use one downsampling layer, followed by two downsampling layers with cross-attention, in which the closure-invariant features adjust convolutional features through the cross-attention mechanism, which conditions the denoising process. On the upsampling path, we implement two upsampling layers with self-attention and one final upsampling layer without attention. By having no cross-attention layers in the upsampling path, the result is a robust conditional denoising network that performs well even with noise from real observations. The latent shape is 4 channels of 16 × 16 grids, which is downsampled from the original 64 × 64 total intensity image grid using a pretrained autoencoder30. The second component of the GenDIReCT architecture is a standard multilayer CNN composed of three sequential downsampling layers, designed to compress a large set of diffusion-sampled images (each considered a separate channel) into a representative data-consistent single-channel image reconstruction. We note that we have experimented with several design variations and found this version to be suitable in all tested cases, but better-performing alternatives for specific datasets may be possible.

Sources indicate that genDIReCT works by learning realistic image characteristics (such as positivity and smooth brightness distribution) from a non-astronomical image training dataset, primarily composed of augmented CIFAR-10 natural images81. The conditional latent diffusion model generates sensible image priors, which the multilayer CNN uses as input to optimize the data likelihood and refine the final image reconstruction. As a generative imaging algorithm, our algorithm has the potential to handle degeneracies and visualize multimodalities in the solution space, although they should not be interpreted as image reconstruction uncertainty under a Bayesian framework. Generally, appearance of minor artefacts in low-sensitivity regions, different levels of smoothness and sharpness or super-resolution variations are acceptable consequences of a diversity in potential solutions to the ill-posed image reconstruction problem. However, methodological and hyperparameter sensitivity, or inability to satisfy the underlying measurements, constitute signs that a reconstruction is not robust. By training on unconvolved ground-truth models, GenDIReCT achieves super-resolved reconstructions and enables generative visualization of structural variations that remain strictly consistent with the observed data. Accordingly, unless otherwise indicated, we present unconvolved GenDIReCT outputs optimized to be consistent with the measurements.

It has been revealed that we have extensively tested our algorithm on synthetic datasets with the EHT or next-generation EHT (ngEHT) array31, as well as non-horizon-scale EHT datasets on active galactic nuclei, 3C 279 and Centaurus A (ref. 32). On synthetic datasets, our algorithm generalizes well to untrained morphologies and maintains >90% image similarity with ground-truth images at signal-to-noise levels well below the datasets of M87*. Moreover, its performance on quantitative metrics is comparable with other state-of-the-art imaging algorithms on the ngEHT total intensity analysis challenge82. For the EHT dataset on 3C 279, our reconstruction is 98% similar to the EHTC ref. 83, reproducing the core-jet morphology across several independent epochs and enabling direct measurement of the superluminal relative proper motion between components in the image domain. For the EHT dataset on Centaurus A, the EHTC ref. 84 is reproduced with 91% similarity with statistically compatible brightness ratios and opening angle between the north and south edge-brightened jet ridges. These extensive tests on real and synthetic data demonstrate that our algorithm is capable of consistently recovering diverse morphological structures, without manual intervention or prescriptive priors.

Before applying to the real data, each trained model is extensively tested on an array of internal validation tests, which include quantifying its performance degradation with out-of-distribution image morphologies and varying levels of data corruption, accounting for the heterogeneous sensitivity of the array32. Only after passing internal validation are the models unblinded on real data to minimize risk of confirmation bias. No alterations are made to the model between the validation procedure and the unblinding, or post-unblinding.

According to recent reports, for this work, we train our machine learning architecture with synthetic data derived using the data coverage from all four 2017 and both 2018/2021 observing days independently, combining the two 2-GHz bands into a single scan-averaged dataset for each epoch. We choose 128 × 128-μas2, 225 × 225-μas2 and 450 × 450-μas2 reconstruction fields, each on 64 × 64-pixel grids as predetermined by the architecture. Generally, we represent the aggregate reconstruction for each dataset by the median of all aligned reconstructions. We find the median representation to be more robust against outliers or source alignment concerns and a better representation of the bulk of individual image reconstructions. The aggregate reconstructions for all datasets and fields of view are shown in Extended Data Fig. 1 alongside EHTC comparison reconstructions, GenDIReCT composites and a median to median absolute deviation (MAD) ratio panel. The median-to-MAD ratio is presented as a visualization of GenDIReCT’s reconstruction confidence31, in which features of low variance relative to the median pixel intensity (that is, high reconstruction confidence) are highlighted with filled contours.

Recent findings suggest that one of the advantages of the generative imaging process of our algorithm is the potential to explore different imaging solution modes. We consider all observation epochs and all fields of view, presenting the median reconstructions from the most populated solution clusters in Extended Data Fig. 2. Image reconstructions are clustered by Hamming distance in their perceptual hash representation32 to illustrate multimodal solutions. Each cluster is also presented with the best data fidelity score in parentheses. Often, more than 50% of all reconstructions reside within the top two most populous and perceptually similar clusters. This clustering behaviour justifies the pixelwise median as a statistically sound and accurate aggregate representation. The M87* clustering results clearly demonstrate that the differences between reconstruction clusters for the observation days with the highest-quality data are in the surface brightness and extent of extraneous amorphous emission surrounding the ring, rather than fundamental changes to the ring structure itself. For other datasets, solution clusters that are not as clearly ring-like are typically of sparse occurrence in comparison with the bulk of reconstructions and exhibit a lower data fidelity score. On all fields of view, there is no non-ring solution that is favoured over ring-like morphology in the share of the reconstructed image population or data fidelity score. The most ambiguous case is that of the 25 April 2018 dataset, which is missing data from the LMT, resulting in reduced image fidelity compared with the 21 April 2018 observations. The absence of LMT-related baselines created a substantial gap in uv coverage at spatial frequencies corresponding to about 1 Gλ, as the LMT–SMT baseline provided the unique long-baseline constraint for structure in this regime33.

Unless otherwise stated, all models described in this work are trained on augmented non-astronomical images from the CIFAR-10 dataset81, as well as simple geometric shapes, such as Gaussians, disks, rings, ellipses and m-rings85 of the first and second orders31. We present an example grid of augmented training images in Extended Data Fig. 3. Once trained, we run the imaging sequence for 96 total GPU hours on a single NVIDIA H100 GPU for each dataset, producing several hundred (about 300) individual image reconstructions, each drawing from 4,096 diffusion samples. The exact number of final image reconstructions depends on data volume. Although our algorithm has been shown to be generalizable to arbitrary source morphologies31, there is a concern that the presence of crescents and rings in the training dataset may be a source of bias for the image reconstruction. Therefore, we also investigate the outcome of training our architecture without geometric shapes in the training dataset and find no notable difference in the image reconstruction (Extended Data Fig. 3).

We use the reduced \({\chi }_{{\rm{CI}}}^{2}\) metric to evaluate the consistency between our image reconstructions with the measurements. The reduced \({\chi }_{{\rm{CI}}}^{2}\) metric is defined as the sum of error-normalized residuals divided by the number of independent data terms,.

in which \({\mathcal{C}}\) is an operator that maps the reconstructed image to its closure invariants, indexed by i, for a fixed observation arrangement and Ci is the corresponding closure invariant of the measurement. The total number of closure invariants is denoted by Nci and \({\sigma }_{i}^{2}\) is the estimated uncertainty on the ith closure invariant. We also define the normalized residual of any data point, i, as \(({\mathcal{C}}{(A)}_{i}-{C}_{i})/{\sigma }_{i}\).

Although propagating the estimated uncertainty from each radio station’s system equivalent flux density is straightforward, the total error on each closure invariant is affected by other sources of systematic errors, including time-dependent errors from long coherent visibility averaging and limitations of the linear error propagation model. Generally, the fractional systematic uncertainty budget of 3C 279 and M87 data is about 5%, which is similar in magnitude as measured inter-pipeline differences2. However, in this work, we present our results without further systematic error tolerance and we consistently use as reference the highest-quality single-day EHT-HOPS-reduced pre-scan-averaged dataset of each observation year (11 April for 2017, 21 April for 2018, 18 April for 2021) when evaluating the reduced \({\chi }_{{\rm{CI}}}^{2}\) to ensure a consistent metric across reconstructions. For these datasets, we illustrate the data fidelity from the best GenDIReCT reconstruction and the xsringauss geometric model in Extended Data Fig. 4. A near-unity reduced \({\chi }_{{\rm{CI}}}^{2}\) value confirms that a reconstruction is self-consistent with the measured closure invariants but does not guarantee that the recovered morphology is correct in an absolute sense, making the reduced \({\chi }_{{\rm{CI}}}^{2}\) a necessary but insufficient metric for an accurate reconstruction.

Sources indicate that in some cases, it is useful to measure the similarity between reconstructions in the image domain, especially when comparing the GenDIReCT reconstructions with the results from the EHTC imaging pipelines. We measure the image-to-image correspondence with the maximum normalized cross-correlation metric, ρNX, which has the advantage of being independent of image translation and total flux scaling. The metric has been widely used to quantitatively measure image similarity, particularly with image reconstructions produced using only closure data terms28,31,32,82. The ρNX metric is defined as.

in which I1 and I2 are two images being compared and the hat operator, \(\hat{I}=(I-\bar{I})/{\sigma }_{I}\), normalizes each image I by its respective flux mean and standard deviation. We denote the forward and inverse Fourier transform as \({\mathcal{F}}\) and \({{\mathcal{F}}}^{-1}\), respectively. The maximum operator ensures that the metric is independent of image translation and it is also useful for aligning separate image reconstructions. To minimize the negative influence of high-frequency artefacts on the maximum normalized cross-correlation, we convolve each image by the fitted clean beam before computing ρNX. Throughout this work, we use ρNX to evaluate the inter-method consistency in resulting image reconstructions, often between the GenDIReCT and EHTC fiducial imaging pipelines or simulated images. As there is no ground-truth reconstruction for M87*, the ρNX metric does not constitute an independent ground-truth validation metric but as an image-domain similarity metric between various imaging algorithms.

Industry observers note that the image-domain feature extraction method presented here follows the framework established by the EHTC in their initial analysis of M87* (ref. 3). We outline the reproduction of this algorithm below. Given any plausibly ring-like image, we first search for the ring centre, (x0, y0), by evaluating all candidate centroid positions for the one that minimizes the normalized radial peak dispersion.

in which \({\bar{r}}_{{\rm{pk}}}(x,y)\) is the radius of peak brightness averaged over all angles, as.

in which I(r, θ; x, y) is the intensity distribution of the image in radial coordinates, centred on (x, y). The dispersion, σr(x, y), is the corresponding standard deviation of rpk(θ; x, y) across all angles, θ. The ring diameter and its uncertainty can then be identified from \({\bar{r}}_{{\rm{pk}}}(x,y)\) and σr(x, y), respectively, given the measured ring centre, (x0, y0).

Once the ring centre is determined, most other characteristic features can be extracted directly from the polar image, including: the ring width wr, orientation η, azimuthal asymmetry A and central brightness fraction fc. The ring width, wr, is determined by measuring the mean FWHM at each radial slice for the given ring centre,.

in which the floor value Ifloor = ⟨I(r = 2rpk, θ)⟩θ is used to correct for any non-zero residual flux outside the ring. The uncertainty on the ring width, σw, is measured by the standard deviation in FWHM across all θ.

The orientation angle, η, of the ring (measured east of north) is the circular mean of the first angular mode from rin = rpk − wr/2 to rout = rpk + wr/2, as.

and the corresponding uncertainty, θη, is the standard deviation of the measured angles for r ∈ [rin, rout].

The azimuthal asymmetry, A, is the mean of the normalized amplitude in the first angular mode from rin to rout, which is.

In a recent development, in which σA is the standard deviation in the measured asymmetry over r ∈ [rin, rout]. Perfect azimuthal symmetry corresponds to a value of A = 0, whereas a delta function with all flux concentrated at a single orientation angle corresponds to a value of A = 1.

Finally, the central brightness fraction, fc, is the ratio between the mean interior depression brightness to the mean ring surface brightness, as.

in which the interior brightness is measured from the average flux in a small disk around the ring centre. Although we do not define an uncertainty for a single measurement of fc, we derive its uncertainty from several measurements across the three different fields of view used in GenDIReCT reconstruction. Figure 2 presents the measured ring diameter and orientation across all datasets considered in this work. We present the measurements for ring width, azimuthal asymmetry and central brightness fraction in Extended Data Fig. 5.

Industry observers note that the EHTC derived ring parameters using the REX module implemented as part of eht-imaging. Ring properties from three different imaging algorithms (DIFMAP37, eht-imaging28 and SMILI66) were reported for the 2017 data3, two Bayesian imaging algorithms (THEMIS86 and Comrade87,88) were included for the 2018 datasets33 and for 2021 data, one further CLEAN-based algorithm (GPCAL89) and two further regularized maximum likelihood algorithms (DOG-HIT67 and MOEA/D (ref. 35)) were added. However, for the 2021 datasets, the EHTC used an alternative template-matching image-domain feature extraction algorithm34. As such, to maintain methodological consistency, we have reproduced a single eht-imaging reconstruction to use as the EHTC reference.

When comparing ring diameter between datasets, image reconstruction algorithms and across multiyear epochs, there is potential for systematic bias arising from the finite-resolution effect, in which variations in ring width can shift the apparent diameter derived from a direct image-domain feature analysis. Recent EHTC analyses use a forward-modelling procedure to mitigate diameter–width degeneracy34. In this work, we choose to maintain methodological consistency across all reconstructions by deriving diameters directly from the image domain without further adjustment. Therefore, the apparent variation observed between imaging algorithms and individual datasets may be influenced by the finite resolution of each imaging method. Despite this, the apparent ring diameter derived from our reconstructions remains self-consistent across all independent datasets.

Recent findings suggest that our complementary Bayesian analysis uses the geometric xsringauss model4,90, which was designed to simulate the appearance of quasi-Kerr black hole accretion disk radio images91. The advantage of geometric modelling is that visibilities can be derived analytically from simple algebraic expressions and fit to the observed measurements, which substantially reduces the computational requirement of modelling compared with complex and highly nonlinear physical models, particularly when applied with Bayesian sampling algorithms. Moreover, as long as the object is plausibly described by the model, Bayesian sampling methods applied with geometric models enable direct inference of key features of interest from the observed object with associated uncertainties. In this section, we provide a brief description of the xsringauss model, the extra components we included to form the model for fitting and the complete analytical visibility function. We develop the BASIS92 software package for Bayesian analysis with the xsringauss model independent from existing software from the EHTC. For the following discussion, we use \({\mathcal{F}}\) to denote the forward Fourier transform operator.

Sources indicate that the xsringauss model is parameterized with the following variables4. The outer disk radius, Rout, and inner disk radius, Rin, create the centralized ‘top-hat crescent’, in which the offset of the inner disk centroid is controlled by the eccentricity, ϵ ∈ [0, 1]. At ϵ = 0, the centres of both disks are co-located at the origin and at the maximum eccentricity, ϵ = 1, the edge of the inner disk meets the edge of the outer disk. The fading parameter, f ∈ [0, 1], controls the surface brightness gradient across the crescent, with the maximum brightness located at the tip of the crescent, at which the crescent width is maximum. When f = 0, the crescent surface brightness is uniform and when f = 1, the surface brightness fades to zero at x = −Rout. Note that we have deliberately adjusted the definition of fading from its original conception90.

The xsringauss model also includes an elliptical Gaussian centred on the inner disk edge, at which the crescent is widest. Its flux is determined by a fraction, fg, of the total flux and its width is set by σe, with axial ratio, ag. The longest axis is always oriented perpendicular to the crescent’s axis of symmetry. A circular Gaussian with flux Vf and width σf centred at x0 represents the floor component internal to the crescent. To complete the base xsringauss model, we blur the image with a circular Gaussian kernel of width σb and rotate the entire image by angle ϕ.

It has been revealed that further components include a larger-scale circular background Gaussian of flux Vbg and width σbg centred at the origin, which is added to include short-spacing flux that is not examined by most of the long-baseline array. Finally, two more nuisance elliptical Gaussians are included, each with independent parameters for flux, width, axial ratio, position angle, angular offsets and Gaussian blur, to capture extraneous amorphous emission that is not modelled by the ring alone and as further degrees of freedom to absorb the effects from measurement errors and systematic uncertainties.

In the Fourier domain, the composite model is a linear combination of elementary components with analytic Fourier transforms. The general Fourier transform (represented by tilde) of a disk with radius R and amplitude V is given by.

In a recent development, in which ρ is the Fourier-domain radial coordinate and J1 is a first-order Bessel function of the first kind. The Fourier transform of a Gaussian with flux V and width σ is,.

In a recent development, in which the Fourier transform of asymmetric Gaussians are determined by exploiting the similarity property of the Fourier transform, that is, \({\mathcal{F}}(G({ax},{by}))=\frac{1}{|{ab}|}\tilde{G}\left(\frac{u}{a},\frac{v}{b}\right)\). Multiplication in the image domain of the crescent by the sloped plane is represented in the Fourier domain by taking a derivative.

in which, for our specific linear slash function, l(x), the corresponding operation in the Fourier domain is.

in which the derivatives of Bessel functions of the first kind, Jn, can be expressed in terms of other Bessel functions, Jn±1, as.

and h is responsible for normalizing the source to the desired total flux, V, which is dependent on the source structure. For the xsringauss model, the normalization factor is.

It has been revealed that each image component can be further independently augmented by translation, rotation and Gaussian blur. In general, image translations are represented with an extra phase term in the Fourier domain, \({{\rm{e}}}^{{\rm{i}}2{\rm{\pi }}({l}_{0}u+{m}_{0}v)}\), in which (l0, m0) denotes the translation in (l, m) coordinates. Image rotation is modelled by a rotation of the uv coordinates. Then, by the convolution theorem, blurring in the image domain with a circular Gaussian kernel is a pointwise multiplication in the Fourier domain by \({{\rm{e}}}^{-{\rm{i}}2{{\rm{\pi }}}^{2}{\sigma }_{{\rm{b}}}^{2}{\rho }^{2}}\), in which σb is the width of the blurring kernel. The final image model and its corresponding analytic Fourier transform is described by 28 parameters. Throughout this work, the xsringauss model is fit to observed data with DYNESTY, a Bayesian dynamic nested sampling algorithm, adopting uniform priors for all parameters. The final fitted image model is formed from the median value of the one-dimensional marginalized posteriors for each parameter. The xsringauss model parameter covariance plot for the highest-quality datasets of 2017 and 2018 is shown in Fig. 3 and we present covariance plots for all other datasets in Extended Data Figs. 6–8. We then apply the image-domain feature extraction analysis on samples from the posterior to measure all characteristic ring parameters (Extended Data Table 1).

Inferring the gravitational radius of the black hole from the measured ring diameter requires independently calibrating each imaging method with synthetic data from simulated GRMHD models of lensed black hole accretion emission4. One common simplification is that the observed size of the reconstructed ring should follow a simple scaling relationship with the gravitational radius, dring = αθg. By calibrating to a large ensemble of simulations with different black hole spins, the EHTC determined the calibration factor, α, from the image-domain feature extraction method to be between 10.67 and 11.01, in which the listed range is the result of variations from different image reconstruction algorithms. For geometric modelling methods, the α calibration factor ranges between 11.01 and 12.06. The median of all α calibrations is α ≃ 11.0, which is the calibration factor used by the EHTC for methods that have not been independently calibrated33. Therefore, we also provisionally apply α ≈ 11.0 as our calibration factor in this study.

The associated theoretical uncertainty in the calibrated scaling factor, which arises from recognizing the dataset as a single sample from a dynamic system with unknown physical properties, is σα = 0.4 (ref. 4). In this work, we also use the mean M87* distance measure from the EHTC, which is \(16.{8}_{-0.7}^{+0.8}\,{\rm{Mpc}}\) (ref. 3) based on studies of high-resolution resolved stellar distribution fluctuations13,93 and the tip of the red giant branch standard candle method14.

Recent findings suggest that the prior expectation for the mass of the central black hole in M87 is primarily sourced from high-quality gas12 and stellar11 dynamical estimates, which measured \({M}_{{\rm{gas}}}=3.{5}_{-0.7}^{+0.9}\times 1{0}^{9}{M}_{\odot }\) and Mstar = (6.6 ± 0.4) × 109 M⊙, respectively. The corresponding gravitational radii are \({\theta }_{{\rm{gas}}}=2.{1}_{-0.4}^{+0.5}\,{\rm{\mu }}{\rm{as}}\) and θstar = 3.9 ± 0.3 μas if we use a distance measure of \(16.{8}_{-0.7}^{+0.8}\,{\rm{Mpc}}\). Using the median α = 11.0 ± 0.4 calibration factor and theoretical uncertainty, the prior ring diameters are \({d}_{{\rm{gas}}}=22.{6}_{-4.7}^{+5.9}\,{\rm{\mu }}{\rm{as}}\) and \({d}_{{\rm{star}}}=42.{7}_{-3.6}^{+3.5}\,{\rm{\mu }}{\rm{as}}\). We therefore estimate a black hole mass of \({M}_{{\rm{BH}}}=6.{5}_{-0.4}^{+0.5}\,(11.0/\alpha )\times 1{0}^{9}\,{M}_{\odot }\) with GenDIReCT’s independently measured mean ring diameter. The full range of α = 10.67–12.06 calibration factors implies an estimated black hole mass in the range MBH = (6.0–6.7) × 109 M⊙. On this basis, we conservatively estimate our black hole mass as MBH = (6.5 ± 0.5) × 109 M⊙.

Sources indicate that to compare the reconstructed composites to synthetic M87* images, we retrieve publicly available GRMHD data (https://thz.astro.illinois.edu/resources.html) from the University of Illinois survey41, which includes fluid data for 1,000 time steps (in Rg/c) in the quasi-stationary equilibrium state and five black hole spin prescriptions (a⁎ = −0.94, −0.5, 0, +0.5, +0.94), evolving under the magnetically arrested disk or standard and normal evolution regimes. In this work, we consider only the magnetically arrested disk fluid models, which is the more likely evolutionary scenario for M87* based on jet power constraints94.

According to recent reports, synthetic 230-GHz images of M87* are produced using the general relativistic radiative transfer IPOLE algorithm40 for all time steps, spins and inclination angles between 5° and 90° with a step size of 1°. Note that we use a coupled electron temperature model characterized by Rhigh = 40, which determines the relationship between the ion and electron temperature. Although Rhigh is a free parameter, the time-averaged magnetically arrested disk images are nearly independent of Rhigh and are sensitive primarily on black hole spin for a fixed inclination94. In this work, we compare all beam-convolved synthetic images with the reconstructed M87* composites in the image domain using the normalized cross-correlation metric after correcting for the observer position angle and making linear adjustments to spatial scale, for which both the rotation and scale adjustments of the synthetic images are chosen independently for each parameter combination of spin, inclination and time step, to maximize the resulting normalized cross-correlation comparison with the composite reconstructions. Simulations in ideal GRMHD models are scale-agnostic, enabling such adjustments to be made without affecting the underlying physics41,95. We also repeat our analysis for Rhigh = 80, presenting the figure in the GenDIReCT repository, and find a mild roughly 2° shift towards lower inclinations.

Post-processed data products or image reconstructions can be located in the GenDIReCT code repository96. 💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 17:03 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 17:05 EST, 13 November 2026.

Mauricio Pochettino already has a fresh injury headache at Manchester United - and he's not even through the door yet.

Patrick Dorgu has been sent home from Denmark duty having failed a series of physical tests.

The full-back missed four Premier League matches in October due to a hamstring injury but came on to provide an assist and score the equaliser in the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa on Sunday.

Now he re-joins an injury list which includes Marcus Rashford, Luke Shaw, Carlos Baleba, and potentially Harry Maguire, with Manuel Ugarte and Benjamin Sesko ruled out longer-term.

Denmark's team doctor Martin Boesen noted: 'We have carried out a series of tests on Dorgu, and he has not performed well enough to be ready to play in the two matches.

'He needs further recovery time after his injury, so we are sending him home for additional rehabilitation.'.

Patrick Dorgu has been sent home fromDenmark duty after failing a series of fitness tests.

It is potentially another thing for incoming manager Mauricio Pochettino to worry about.

Dorgu, 22, will miss matches against Portugal and Norway in the Nations League.

Pochettino will hope Dorgu makes a quick recovery as he seeks to get Manchester United back on track.

United, who sit 18th in the Premier League, agreed to pay more than £10million to prise Pochettino and his staff away from the United States national team.

Pochettino has signed a two-and-a-half-year deal to replace Michael Carrick and will get down to business after his final matches in charge of the USA against Haiti on Saturday and Wednesday.

The former Southampton, Tottenham, and Chelsea boss broke down in tears as he began his farewell and admitted that he couldn’t turn down the ‘dream’ job of Manchester United head coach.

Flanked by US Soccer Federation bosses at the team’s headquarters in Georgia, an emotional Pochettino wiped away tears as he thanked the players and staff.

According to recent reports, ‘I haven't prepared a speech, I'm talking with my heart,’ he mentioned. ‘It's difficult for me to talk now because I am a very emotional guy.

Recent findings suggest that ‘When these moments arrive, it is always tough. Normally it is the opposite – you have been sacked! You cry because you want to stay.

‘I think it was one of the most difficult decisions of our career, but you have to move forward.

‘Not too many opportunities can happen in your career with a side like Manchester United. That is difficult to turn down when it arrives.

‘In some part it’s a very sad decision, in another part we are professional and we are trying to make our dreams come true. We are excited for that step forward.'.

The 54-year-old Argentine revealed that United first made contact on Sunday after the 4-4 draw in Carrick’s final game left the club in the relegation zone.

‘I never remarked I wanted to go back in the Premier League,’ said Pochettino, whose first game in charge of United will be against Liverpool at Anfield a week on Sunday.

‘All of this was so quick because we arrived here last Friday and on Sunday afternoon this type of situation started to appear. There was some contact. When things became bigger, they are very sensitive.

‘We were very transparent with the federation and they understand the situation. The decision between US Soccer and Man United to agree to continue for these two games will not change our commitment.

‘That decision was between the three parties but, of course if Man United agreed different terms, I need to respect that.’.

There will be some games where Mikel Arteta has no choice but to tweak the XI, rest some tired legs and give his second-choice attackers the chance – although given the option he may wish to pick the same team every week.

According to recent reports, the three big guns of his attack were primed and ready to come on in the next break in play when Arsenal at last broke through in this, their second Champions League league phase game of the season against some stubborn opposition from Ligue 1. Lille had sat deep against an Arsenal attack without Bukayo Saka, Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz, and the French club were past the hour when it all finally broke.

Recent findings suggest that that was a superb finish from Jurrien Timber who, with two touches, demonstrated that in the modern era even defenders are capable of the kind of moments of skill and composure that we once assumed were only within the capacity of the best attackers. He gave Arsenal the lead just as Mikel Arteta had decided he had seen enough from some of his second-choice attackers – Viktor Gyokeres, Noni Madueke and Mikel Merino. They had created some chances and at times looked promising, but as soon as the major three were on the difference was obvious.

In a recent development, this touch and finish from Jurriën Timber 😮‍💨 Arsenal lead against Lille! 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/WPrcA5ZrQ1 https://t.co/L2B6YsNDXo.

According to recent reports, “We had moments in the game in the first half … [when] we arrived in very dangerous positions,” Arteta remarked. “With a lot of advantage, our technical quality wasn’t good enough to deliver moments of real threat and especially to be able to sustain the attack, so we allowed certain transitions.” He said that he made some changes at half-time, as managers are wont to do, and that things improved but the real change was clear when he made the substitutions.

“It was a joy to watch,” Arteta noted. “The three goals were unbelievable, the connections, the timings, the quality they delivered to score. Three different players and a lot of players participating in those goals, so overall very, very happy.” He had played Myles Lewis-Skelly at left-back again to give Riccardo Calafiori a rest. Saka had been ill during the week and not in a position to start.

It has been revealed that in the opposing technical area was Davide Ancelotti, the 37-year-old son of Carlo, with his father’s trademark slow amble to the edge of the technical area. Young Ancelotti had drilled his team well, but once they were exposed to the high-pace recovery and sharp passing geometry of the Arsenal substitutes there was to be no coming back. Saka made the second for Eberechi Eze who had started the game on the left and the Arsenal No 7 scored the third himself. The home fans sang again about being champions of England and they certainly looked the part.

It didn't take Arsenal long to double their lead ⚡️ Eberechi Eze scores to make it 2-0 🎯 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/WPrcA5ZrQ1 https://t.co/BVMieESgbi.

It has been revealed that it took a while. Arteta got ever more sour in his dealings with Richard Hempel, the giant German fourth official. Bruno Guimarães hustled as best he could in midfield and might have won a penalty. But essentially Arsenal lacked the subtle attacking edge that distinguishes the best from the rest in this competition. You could see it immediately in the way that Odegaard hunted for the ball for the second goal and then turned urgently to attack Lille. The third goal was a passing sequence from Saka to Odegaard to Havertz and back to Saka for the finish.

The Arsenal players wore black armbands to mark the passing, aged 94, of Ken Friar, the club’s life vice-president. He had served the club from 1945 to 2014 and was variously club secretary, managing director and a driving force in building the stadium in which they now play. Even Arteta, no sentimentalist, insisted on beginning his press conference with a tribute.

Sources indicate that for Arteta’s players, there will be a much bigger test than this one in Munich next week against Bayern. Arsenal have already won in Naples but a victory at Bayern would be significant beyond that. Arsenal have won all but one of their 10 games this season – that major defeat at the Amex Stadium, almost one month ago. They clearly have another gear to go to when required although ideally, Arteta would not always have to ask it of the same players. The club have spent too much on this squad not to be able to trust the understudies.

Madueke did at least end the game with an assist. Of Saka’s understudy, Arteta said: “When you talk about players being clinical – what is clinical? Clinical sometimes means that they score one in every 500. It’s about generating volume and more actions and getting him into the good position because he will decide matches.”.

No goals for Gyokeres this season and a general acceptance that the time for persevering with him has passed. It could be ever-dwindling returns for him in terms of game-time as the season goes. Coming off the bench for Lille in the second half was the unmistakable Olivier Giroud, now 40 and more than 14 years on since he signed for Arsenal from Montpellier. He was given a warm welcome by the home fans and, later, an equally warm farewell despite the Chelsea years in the interim. He was a much better player than Gyokeres in an era when Arsenal were in decline.

Guimarães had two chances in the first half. Lille’s Japan international Ayase Ueda had a goal disallowed for offside. Guimarães would have a further penalty appeal before the hour as Arteta began to consider the substitutions.

Arteta starts his press conference with a tribute to Ken Friar: "There are people in football clubs that create an identity, create values and have a vision to create a future. The legacy that Ken is going to leave, to all of us and to our club, is going to be forever.".

The moment we started to do that better, we could counter-press, and start to play into the opposition’s box, and with the quality that we have we made a real difference there.

I had some moments in the first half but second half I had more. First touch was good, which was half the job, and then Noni [Madueke] was screaming “shoot” so I thought OK I have to shoot. And then yeah it went in nice.

In a recent development, I wasn’t thinking too much. I saw the goal and thought I need to shoot. We needed that first goal, we were playing well just needed the goal. Happy to get that for the team.

Michael Olise was sent off in Bayern Munich’s draw at Viking, meaning he will miss next week’s game against Arsenal at the Allianz Arena.

Since returning to the competition under Arteta in 2023, they have won all 12 home group-stage or league-phase matches, conceding just three goals.

Including knock-out games, Arsenal have conceded just eight goals in 20 home matches, keeping 15 clean sheets.

Four of those goals came in effective dead rubbers against PSV in the 2025 last-16 (after Arsenal won 7-1 in Eindhoven) and against Kairat Almaty in the final game of last season’s league phase.

So in home Champions League games that matter, they have conceded just four goals in 18 matches: Serge Gnarby and Harry Kane for Bayern in the 2024 quarter-final, Ousmane Dembele in the 2025 semi-final and Lennart Karl for Bayern in last season’s league phase.

Two wins from two in the Champions League for Arsenal, joining Sporting and Barcelona as the teams with a 100 per cent record.

Recent findings suggest that it’s very difficult. You come across very special people in life and Ken was certainly one of them. He’s an absolute legend of this football club. I think he’s the soul of this football club and someone that has given his life to this club.

This stadium wouldn’t be built if not for him. So, very sad news. The legacy he’s leaving is immense and our thoughts are with his family and we want to pay a proper tribute when we can.

It has been revealed that our players will be wearing black armbands this evening in memory of Ken Friar OBE. Rest in peace, Ken ❤️ https://t.co/xf91JABjrD.

In a recent development, lille’s manager is Davide Ancelotti, the son of Carlo, and you would assume he has picked up a few tips and tricks from his dad about success in this competition. Carlo, after all, has won the European Cup on five separate occasions. This is Davide’s second job as a manager, following a spell at Brazilian side Botafogo.

In a recent development, some of Bukayo Saka’s finishing has been wayward so far this season, but the volume of chances coming his way bodes well. At this fledgling stage of the season, only Erling Haaland is averaging more non-penalty expected goals per 90 minutes in the Premier League.

As Sam Dean explores in this piece, Arteta seems to be encouraging Saka to take up more central positions inside the box.

It has been revealed that sam writes: “Is Saka becoming a proper penalty-box predator? It is too early to say for certain but it is absolutely clear that he is taking up different positions, closer to the opponents’ goal, this season. Not only when the ball is on the left flank, but also when Arsenal are attacking through midfield.”.

Saka starts among the substitutes this evening, but will play his part towards the end of the game.

Lille are considering legal ⁠action after defender Tiago Santos suffered a serious knee injury following an “uncontrolled and dangerous” tackle in Saturday’s match ‌against Le Havre.

Santos, 24, suffered a ruptured anterior cruciate ligament and meniscal tear in his right knee and was carried off the pitch on a stretcher after being tackled by Le Havre midfielder Amir Richardson during the first half of Lille’s 1-0 victory.

The referee gave a foul for the tackle but did not concern Richardson with a caution.

Lille said the ‌tackle merited ‌a red card ⁠and that they had asked the league’s governing body (LFP) to refer the matter to its disciplinary committee. The club are also seeking an explanation of ⁠the video review process undertaken by match officials.

It has been revealed that “LOSC is exploring all possible legal avenues and reserves the right to take any legal action necessary to obtain compensation for its losses,” the ​club said. “It will support Tiago in ‌any steps he decides to take to defend his rights.”.

The artist Northbanksy has plumped for another Oasis-inspired dig at Manchester City, this time with Rui Pinto taking centre stage, the man whose leaked emails kicked off the Premier League investigation into City’s financial affairs.

A consequence of Piero Hincapie’s injury on Saturday (he hurt his ankle in a cool-down session after the game, embarrassingly) is that Myles Lewis-Skelly is seemingly now the backup left-back. Arsenal can’t trust Riccardo Calafiori’s body to play two games in a week and are clearly saving him for Premier League action on the weekend. Lewis-Skelly has been so impressive in midfield that it must be frustrating to change position now.

In a recent development, bakwa is on loan from Nottingham Forest, while those at the Emirates with long memories will remember that Nabil Bentaleb played for Spurs. Only the knowledgeable shall boo.

Lille XI: Özer; Perraud, Alexsandro, Ngoy, Goffi; Bentaleb, André; Mukau, Haraldsson, Bakwa; Ueda.

Subs: Gill, Srdanovic, Giroud, Sahraoui, Kjaergaard, Onal, Kouassi, Verdonk, Cossier, Perrin, Diaoune, Sajous.

Bukayo Saka, Kai Havertz and Martin Odegaard drop to the bench, so some rotation from Arteta with a weekend trip to Nottingham Forest in mind, a venue where Arsenal have drawn 0-0 on their last two visits.

Arsenal XI: Raya; Timber, Konsa, Gabriel, Lewis-Skelly; Bruno, Rice; Madueke, Merino, Eze; Gyokeres.

Subs: Meslier, Kepa, White, Mosquera, Salmon, O’Neill, Hashi, Saka, Odegaard, Havertz, Dowman.

Recent findings suggest that will Olivier Giroud receive a warm welcome back to the Emirates Stadium? The Frenchman spent six years as an Arsenal player but burned a few bridges when he left the club for Chelsea, and then celebrated wildly when Chelsea beat Arsenal in the Europa League final of 2019. Now 40, Giroud has shown remarkable longevity and is unquestionably one of the best strikers of his generation. But can he hurt this formidable Arsenal defence? It’s a tough ask.

Olivier Giroud back at the Emirates ❤️ https://t.co/TPBgcNDsVW.

Industry observers note that arsenal pay tribute to one of the club’s greatest custodians this evening following the news of Ken Friar’s death aged 92. Friar worked in various roles at the club across more than 70 years, and a bridge from Drayton Park to Emirates Stadium is named in his honour.

A statue at the end of the bridge is a nod to the chance meeting the 11-year-old Friar had with Arsenal manager George Allison in 1945, while playing football outside Highbury with his friends.

Industry observers note that as Sam Dean wrote earlier today, finishing the story: “Allison was so impressed by Friar’s enthusiasm that he told him to report to his office at 9am the next day. Friar did as he was instructed and his reward was a job offer: he became a messenger at the stadium on match days. He was paid 12 and a half pence per week.”.

Friar was a long-serving member of the Arsenal board, before stepping back in 2020 and becoming life president.

Arsenal’s players will wear black armbands.

A post shared by Sam Dean (@samjdean_tel).

After signing his newly introduced Arsenal contract last week, Mikel Arteta described May’s Champions League final defeat as “poison in his veins,” and last season’s campaign demonstrated the benefits of finishing top of the league phase.

Arsenal enjoyed home second legs all the way through to the final after winning eight from eight, and in a 50:50 draw they fell into a considerably kinder bracket.

Sometimes it can be hard to gauge the importance of these league-phase matches, but Arteta will strive for another perfect record to give Arsenal the best possible chance of going deep in the competition again.

Fixtures against Bayern Munich and Real Madrid are likely to determine whether Arsenal finish in the top two, but there is still a job to be done against Lille this evening.

Arsenal have played against 10 different French opponents in European competition but have never faced Lille, who are managed by Davide Ancelotti, son of five-time Champions League winner Carlo.

Lille sell their best players every summer. After finishing third in Ligue 1 last season they lost Ayyoub Bouaddi and Matias Fernandez-Pardo to Manchester City and Newcastle United for a combined £130m. They have claimed 10 points from their first five league games of the season and led Paris St-Germain 2-0 before being pegged back in stoppage time.

Sources indicate that leading the line for Lille is 40-year-old Olivier Giroud, who scored 105 Arsenal goals in 235 appearances between 2012 and 2018. After leaving the Emirates, Giroud went on to score against Arsenal for Chelsea in the 2019 Europa League final, but he can still expect a warm reception.

It has been revealed that arsenal’s home record in the Champions League has been formidable since they returned to the competition under Arteta in 2023. They have won all 11 home group-stage or league-phase matches, conceding just three goals (two of those were shipped against Kairat Almaty in a dead rubber).

Arteta’s scope for rotation has been reduced by injuries to Piero Hincapie and Martin Zubimendi, but tonight’s game should offer Eberechi Eze and Viktor Gyokeres a chance to impress, while Jurrien Timber needs minutes to build his fitness.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that the Rams will have eyes on the January transfer window as an opportunity to strengthen their depleted squad.
  • Here, we put forward three summer targets who Derby County should have back on their radar.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, derby County have had a tough season, but entered the November international break on a high by beating Bolton Wanderers in their last game. It buys John Eustace more time in the dugout as DCFC look to turn around their fortunes.

Industry observers note that the Rams will have eyes on the January transfer window as an opportunity to strengthen their depleted squad. Injuries have forced them into the free agents market, signing Shane Duffy and Jack Robinson, but more long-term fixes can be found by targeting some of the summer’s targets who slipped through the fingers.

Here, we put forward three summer targets who Derby County should have back on their radar.

Industry observers note that derby County were among the clubs interested in signing Mattie Pollock from Championship rivals Watford in the summer. However, he ended up staying at Vicarage Road and was named as club captain.

Recent findings suggest that pollock has publicly spoken about how earning the captaincy made him feel confident that he was in the right place. But, with the Hornets struggling and doubts surrounding their long-term direction amid the Pozzo family’s ownership, a fresh opportunity could be tempting this January.

The Rams may not be in a better place in the league, but there is more hope for long-term prosperity at Pride Park than there is at Vicarage Road. Paying to sign Pollock as the present and future of their backline would be a statement of intent and a big step in the right direction away from signing older players.

Another player on the Derby County radar was Anis Mehmeti, but like Pollock, he stayed put. The Albanian had wide Championship interest after Ipswich Town’s rise to the Premier League, but he decided to compete for his place at Portman Road.

Industry observers note that that has not panned out as hoped, and the attacking midfielder should look to make a winter exit. Mehmeti is a proven star in the Championship, offering a dual threat of goals and assists as a No. 10 or on the left-wing.

Industry observers note that he could be the creative spark Eustace’s Rams side needs. Entrusting him with an influential role in the team could help DCFC win the race for his signature, as other second tier sides are sure to be interested.

Last but not least is James Tavernier, who some supporters may view as an underwhelming addition. Granted, he is now 35, but the experience and leadership he would bring to an unstable right-back position would not go amiss.

Tavernier only joined Maccabi Tel Aviv in the summer, but his deal is up at the end of the season, and he could be tempted by the chance to end his career back in England. He would also bring impressive set-piece ability with him, offering Derby County a much-needed route to chances.

Tavernier might not be a long-term option but it would take the pressure off a struggling Max Johnston and decrease the reliance on the likes of Joe Ward and Ryan Nyambe.

Bradford City takeover: Everything we know right now

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Bradford City are being linked to a potential takeover by a Thai-based consortium, so here's a round-up of the latest on whether this move might come off.
  • The international break couldn't have come at a better time for Bradford City.
  • Following an exceptional start to the season, the departure of manager Graham Alexander to Preston North End at the start of October hit the club hard, and they went into the break with just one win from their last six league matches and having slipped from the top of the League One table to eighth place, having replaced Alexander with the former Wycombe Wanderers manager Michael Duff.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bradford City are being linked to a potential takeover by a Thai-based consortium, so here's a round-up of the latest on whether this move might come off.

The international break couldn't have come at a better time for Bradford City.

Following an exceptional start to the season, the departure of manager Graham Alexander to Preston North End at the start of October hit the club hard, and they went into the break with just one win from their last six league matches and having slipped from the top of the League One table to eighth place, having replaced Alexander with the former Wycombe Wanderers manager Michael Duff.

Sources indicate that but losing Alexander may not even be the biggest change to be coming to Bradford City this season. It's been rumoured that a Thai-based consortium are considering launching a bid to buy the club from current owner Stefan Rupp, with the group having been attracted by the club's recent upward trajectory and potential, given the size of attendances they were attracting, even while the team was misfiring in League Two.

This isn't the first time since Rupp purchased the club in 2016 that there has been an attempt to wrest Bradford City from his control, so here's a round-up of what's been noted about ongoing reported interest in buying them, and what it could mean for a club who previously slipped from the Premier League to League Two in just six years, between 2001 and 2007.

A report from journalist Alan Nixon on Sunday morning has reopened conjecture that the Bradford City owner Stefan Rupp could be set to sell the club after ten years of ownership. Nixon confirmed on his Patreon that "Bradford City are a surprise target for a Thai-based group" who have been considering buying into the EFL.

Nixon confirmed that the prospective bidders have shown interest in buying a club before, and that, "Bradford could be for sale at the right price and the Thais, who have an intermediary with inside knowledge, are considering an official offer.".

In a recent development, do you think Bradford City would be better off under upcoming ownership? Let us know in the comments below!

But before anything else, any newly introduced owners will have to get a takeover past Rupp, and that might not be completely straightforward. The German has been reported to be more open to selling since the club were promoted from League Two in 2025, with The Athletic's Matt Slater reporting in March 2026 that, "Rupp has been listening to offers for years but has showing a bit more leg ever since last season’s promotion.".

Recent findings suggest that rupp has, however, said in the past that he won't sell up to just anybody. In 2021, he rejected an offer from the US cryptocurrency investors WAGMI United. They instead turned their attention to Crawley Town but, since completing their takeover of the Sussex-based club in April 2022, Crawley's position has waned considerably, with the Red Devils presently propping up the rest of the EFL and six points from safety.

Rumours that Bradford City could be sold have provoked a strong reaction from fans of the club, so here's a selection of what they've had to say.

This poll of fans highlighted a majority of those who voted being against any takeover of their club:.

While this fan doesn't believe that these rumours should be a surprise to anybody:.

This fan is concerned over what's happened at several other clubs who've come under far eastern ownership:.

And this fan believes that Stefan Rupp has already demonstrated that he is the owner that Bradford City need:.

Their recent slump in League One notwithstanding, the direction of travel that Bradford City have undertaken over the last couple of seasons makes them a prime target for those seeking to buy into the English game.

It has been revealed that for years, it felt as though the Bantams had everything bar the team. They had a stadium which is fit for Premier League football, and attendances were extremely healthy, even when the team wasn't performing especially well in League Two. On top of this, being the only professional football club in a city of half a million people gives the opportunity for further growth, should they continue to rise through the divisions.

Under Alexander, the team was finally successful, winning promotion back to League One in 2025 following an absence of six years, and their first season back hinted that the Bantams weren't done either, with the team finishing in a highly creditable fourth place before losing 2-0 on aggregate to Bolton Wanderers in the semi-finals of the play-offs.

But there is one word in Alan Nixon's report which may cause Bradford fans to worry a little about the nature of the group who are now being linked with the club. Nixon described this consortium as "speculators", and that will raise concerns about the motives of this group among some.

According to recent reports, there isn't anywhere near enough detail about this group to be able to draw too many inferences about their intentions for the club, though it's previously been reported that they are connected to the former owners of Oxford United. But "speculators" is a loaded word, and there may be concern over whether they will have their own interests at heart or those of the club should they take over.

And when speaking to the Bradford Telegraph & Argus at the end of June, Rupp confirmed that, "You get requests from time to time but they are tyre kickers, people without money, wannabe football club owners, or people you simply don't like," and that, "I'm the keeper of the keys and I would never hand it over to somebody where I have the impression he can't do any better.".

Recent findings suggest that the sale price, should it be the same as it was reported to be earlier in 2026, would be unlikely to be too much of a sticking point. The Athletic's report in March suggested that £10 million could be enough to persuade him to sell, with Bradford owning neither their own ground nor their training ground, but such a sum could still only be considered a drop in the ocean, were the club to ascend to the Championship or beyond.

Still in the FA Cup, and with an EFL Cup quarter-final at Manchester City to look forward to in the middle of December, Bradford City remain in a better condition on the pitch than they have been for years, and the substantial irony of their current position is that this very success may push up their sale price. Stefan Rupp has said before that he will only sell the club to the right buyer, but the true test of his principles may come when the rumours cease and concrete offers start to land on his desk.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Rotherham United man Denzel Hall replaced Kyle Ming in a right wing-back role at the break and helped see out a vital win.
  • It could have been an even more memorable night for the hosts as they were three to the good by the hour-mark.
  • Hall isn’t the only Rotherham United player to represent Jamaica, with Brandon Cover also featuring for the Caribbean nation.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rotherham United man Denzel Hall replaced Kyle Ming in a right wing-back role at the break and helped see out a vital win. The Reggae Boyz put themselves in pole position to reach the CONCACAF Nations League semi-finals ahead of Wednesday’s second leg, by winning the first tie 3-2.

It could have been an even more memorable night for the hosts as they were three to the good by the hour-mark. But, Mexico staged a late fightback to reduce the deficit, courtesy of goals from Gilberto Mora and Julian Quinones.

Hall isn’t the only Rotherham United player to represent Jamaica, with Brandon Cover also featuring for the Caribbean nation. However, he missed out on a call-up this time around.

This was Hall’s first call-up having been granted a Jamaican passport in October 2025 and looked set to play a key role in the final stages of their FIFA World Cup qualifying campaign last season.

According to recent reports, hall did feature for the Netherlands at youth level, representing them from U15 to U17, having been born in Rotterdam. But, the wealth of talent ahead of him blocked his pathway into the senior side.

With Jamaican heritage through his father, the Rotherham United man was eligible to switch international allegiance and did so last year to get a taste of international football on the biggest stage.

Despite his impressive performances in a struggling Millers side last season, the 25-year-old was overlooked for his first two opportunities to join the squad as the Reggae Boyz suffered a defeat to DR Congo in March to deny them a place in the World Cup.

Taking the less-travelled route from Rotterdam to Rotherham last summer, Hall signed from Heerenveen but was expected to leave ahead of the new season following their relegation.

According to recent reports, cardiff City and Preston North End were reportedly interested in the versatile defender but neither deal materialised. Since, he has started in all of Rotherham United’s League Two games this term.

A rotten run of form has left them in 22nd place with their last league victory coming against Northampton Town nearly two months ago, although progressing past Bromley in the FA Cup last time out could help inspire an upturn in form.

Hall’s performance against Mexico means he could earn his first start in Wednesday’s second-leg, with his athleticism and work rate in a wing-back role making him a valuable option to call upon.

Also in contention for Rotherham’s trip to high-flying Grimsby Town this weekend, Hall is set to play a key role in trying to help the Millers avoid relegation to non-league for the first time in their history.

Industry observers note that ibrahimovic wrote a foreword in the book, which has been relayed by MilanNews. The RedBird Capital senior advisor spoke about just how much the club means to him, after his two spells as a player and now his time as an executive.

It has been revealed that “Milan are the most key team in my life. And it’s also the only one that convinced me to return. In my career, I’ve worn legendary shirts, played in wonderful cities, and won everywhere. But Milan was something different,” he remarked.

Industry observers note that “It was the only club that truly drew me back, the only one where I felt the need to start over. Convincing Zlatan to return isn’t easy. It’s not easy for anyone. Yet, with Milan, it’s happened more than once.

Because starting an adventure with a club can happen. Returning a second time, and then again, means that the club and its fans have become part of you.

“AC Milan are the most successful Italian club at international level, but it’s not just a collection of trophies. It’s an identity. It’s a way of being in football and in the world. Wherever it goes, it leaves a mark. And those who join AC Milan, sometimes, never leave.”.

It has been revealed that ibrahimovic signed the first time in August 2010 after an experience at Barcelona that wasn’t a positive one, and he helped Milan to the Scudetto with a 14-goal haul. He won the Capocannoniere the next season, doubling that tally.

He returned in 2019 and scored 25 goals in 37 appearances in his first two campaigns, securing a return to European competitions. At the end of his third season, the climb was complete: the Rossoneri won their 19th league title.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the two Bristol clubs don't meet often, yet their rivalry is one of the fiercest in the English game. Right now, though, City and Rovers fans are united in their dislike of their current managers.

We're right in the midst of sacking season in the EFL, and both Michael Skubala and Steve Evans are edging closer to the trapdoor, having failed thus far, with both sides having lofted expectations ahead of the campaign.

Bristol City have had those expectations since their run to the play-offs under Liam Manning in 2024/25, but a transfer window which saw plenty of investment into the playing squad, with the likes of Dom Ballard, Lorent Tolaj, Lisav Eissat and others arriving, has only stoked that anticipation that they could make a run towards the top eight.

Meanwhile, all the good feeling that Steve Evans created in the latter stages of last season and in the first few weeks of this year has dissipated, with the Gas routinely beaten and looking over their shoulders, which wasn't the strategy at all this year.

While Bristol City fans would like to have maintained their play-off level in the last couple of years, there was some potential leeway regarding some form of a project over the summer.

The Robins had a little shake-up in the board over the past year, with Charlie Boss appointed CEO in February, a few months after lifelong fan Richard Scudamore became a member of the board and Sporting Director James Ellis arrived this past summer. This is their first full season at the club.

Each day there are five current or former EFL players to identify. For each one you’ll see their senior clubs in the order they played for them. Loan spells are left out.

According to recent reports, you get four guesses per player. Every wrong guess unlocks a clue: first their position, then their nationality, then their initials.

Recent findings suggest that get it first time for 4 points, then 3, 2 and 1. The best possible score is 20. A newly introduced set of players arrives at midnight.

Turn on JavaScript to play Career Path.

Bringing in Michael Skubala and investing in some promising players from League One and abroad indicated that this would be a multi-year project to try and get into the Premier League, but as it stands, Bristol City are sleepwalking towards the third tier, winning just two of their last 10 games.

More importantly, though, Skubala's brand of football isn't giving fans the belief that things will get better. They've scored just four goals at Ashton Gate, and lost their last home game 5-0 against Norwich City. To many, that was the final straw.

Evidently, Robins fans aren't having Skubala in charge anymore, and once you lose the supporters, it's hard to see a route back.

While Michael Skubala's situation is very much a project yet to get going, the fall-off at Bristol Rovers for Steve Evans these last couple of months has been head-scratching and rather alarming.

It was just six months ago that Evans was celebrating amongst the fans in their 4-0 win over Cheltenham Town, marking their seventh successive victory at the Memorial Ground and their eighth straight in league action. If he went into the crowd now, they'd probably have a different reaction.

The Gas were many's pre-season favourites in League Two this year after they ended last season with 11 wins in their final 14 games, and they started this term with four wins from five. Since then, it's been one win and eight defeats in 10.

The credit that Evans built up through the latter stages of last season has left the bank, and Gas fans are calling for a change.

Saturday's home defeat against Chesterfield leaves Bristol Rovers sitting 18th in League Two, with the main concerns coming from the effort of the players during this dry spell of form.

Bristol City made their decision over the international break. With fans calling for Michael Skubala's head, CEO Charlie Boss sent a message of confidence towards their head coach.

Regardless of what Robins fans think, there can be some admiration that the hierarchy hasn't panicked immediately and is willing to give Skubala time to try and turn the ship around and oversee the multi-year project he signed up for in the summer.

The schedule doesn't get any easier for Bristol City after the break, though, with Middlesbrough, Wrexham, West Brom and Swansea City coming up in their next four games.

Recent findings suggest that city fans are going to have to stick with Skubala through this difficult period and try to will their side on to collect some points. If not, the Robins could be in a relegation battle as we head towards Christmas, and a sacking then would only be seen as a decision made weeks too late at Ashton Gate.

While there hasn't been a direct vote of confidence at board level, Steve Evans may still have a small amount of credit left to try and turn this dreadful form around at the Memorial Stadium.

Evans' predecessor, Darrell Clarke, was sacked after losing 10 straight league games, so the higher-ups have shown patience where it may have been running thin in the stands previously.

Do you think both Michael Skubala and Steve Evans will be in their respective jobs by 2027? Let us know in the comments.

There's also the possibility that things don't get better without Evans in the dugout, who has achieved success nearly everywhere he's been, especially in League Two, with him getting Rotherham United and Stevenage promoted from this level in the past.

In a recent development, right now, both sets of fans in Bristol want their current head coaches to leave, but it doesn't seem like that will happen anytime soon. Only time will tell whether those decisions are the correct ones.
