📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

QPR have enjoyed uplifting progression under Julien Stephan into contention for a play-off place in the Championship this season, but the West Londoners may now be applying some focus to resisting the threat of transfer interest in one particular starlet from Italian giants AC Milan following fresh reports.

The Hoops have transitioned from mid-table mediocrity to Championship promotion hopefuls after completing what was widely felt to be an exciting summer transfer window, which included the arrivals of Pierce Charles, Dennis Cirkin, Glen Kamara and Tariq Lamptey.

As such, QPR find themselves positioned in eighth place amid the ongoing November international break and, having lost just two of their last ten matches against automatic promotion hopefuls in Birmingham City and Southampton, Stephan's outfit appear firmly capable of continuing to fight it out for a top-eight finish.

Away from the pitch, however, QPR are now facing a latest worry as AC Milan and others hone in their transfer sights on one Loftus Road star who Stephan's players would certainly hate to see depart out of W12.

As reported by Sky Sports' Anthony Joseph on Monday afternoon, QPR prodigy Leon Scarlett is attracting interest from mainland Europe in a development that will leave Hoops supporters worried about losing the club's top young prospect.

Indeed, Joseph has claimed that both AC Milan and Eintracht Frankfurt have already expressed an interest in the highly-rated 17-year-old's services ahead of the looming January transfer window, with the continental pair reportedly continuing to monitor his situation at Loftus Road.

Scarlett, who has made six senior appearances for the second-tier play-off hopefuls to date since heading across London to join from Arsenal in January of last year, has enjoyed a meteoric rise and is regarded as a future star in the making.

The talented winger made his debut in a 3-0 defeat at Ipswich Town on the final day of the previous season before climbing up Stephan's ranks throughout the summer and appearing in current-campaign clashes against Charlton Athletic, West Bromwich Albion, Preston North End, Derby County and Birmingham.

Scarlett has made quite the impression in some of those encounters, too, and while the ex-Arsenal academy starlet is yet to open his professional goalscoring account, QPR fans are desperate to see more appearances in the coming weeks and months.

That could change if either AC Milan or Frankfurt seal a swoop, though, with Scarlett's star only rising after collecting a pair of caps with Wales' U21 set-up for good measure.

Scarlett has earned rave reviews from supporters, players and coaches alike since being fast-tracked into Stephan's first-team fold, which is precisely why the R's will be eager to avoid losing such an exciting young asset.

Stephan, who knows a thing or two about developing top-grade talent after previously coaching world stars such as Eduardo Camavinga, 2025 Ballon D'Or winner Ousmane Dembele and Manchester City wing-king Jeremy Doku at Rennes, has already talked up Scarlett's quality.

In a recent development, the Frenchman has been keeping a close eye on the Welsh youth international's ever-accelerating development throughout the year, and was left impressed after promoting him to the senior squad in the closing stages of last term. Stephan told the Hounslow Herald: "The last game (Scarlett) did for the U21s, he did very well.

Recent findings suggest that "I saw him in a cup game with the U18s earlier in the season and he did a good first half. So I just wanted to see him during the session with us (the first team). And during the session, he did well.".

Collect every point to win the round. Don’t let Neil Warnock catch you.

Sources indicate that arrow keys or WASD to move. P to pause, M to mute.

Swipe on the pitch or use the pad to move.

Scarlett has excited his teammates, too, with club captain Jimmy Dunne a notable example.

Speaking at a fans forum event back in September, the popular defender also explained: "Just watching Leon Scarlett today he’s so impressive, so bright, and so positive.

"You want to see him do well and thrive.".

Only time will tell, of course, whether the likes of Dunne, Stephan and QPR as a whole can see Scarlett reach his full potential at Loftus Road and become the beneficiaries of the wide-man's talent and footballing ceiling - or if a larger European club will end up reaping the rewards instead.

It's clear that QPR could just need to implement some form of action in order to guarantee Scarlett's longer-term future, with the prodigious forward surely capable of becoming a first-team regular in the next twelve months.

The worry right now will be that Scarlett remains contracted to the scholarship deal he penned under two years ago to join from Arsenal, and can be easily poached until he agrees to sign professional terms.

QPR would surely love to put that sort of contract on the table for Scarlett, and will need to find out exactly where the player's own desires lie in light of emerging interest from a juggernaut of European football and one of the continent's premiere talent-developers in Frankfurt.

QPR fans, how do you feel about AC Milan and Eintracht Frankfurt's interest in Leon Scarlett? Are you worried that the exciting winger will leave Loftus Road for bigger things already? Let us know your thoughts in the comments below!

Either way, the Championship side are susceptible to losing Scarlett before his Hoops career has really taken off, and it's no surprise that vultures are circling in an effort to exploit that situation and prize away the teenage prodigy.

Wolves and Southampton will wince at new £70m transfer revelation

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (919 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways

  • Only five points separates all three clubs after 15 games, with Middlesbrough only second on goal difference, whilst Wolves sit two places and just one point behind Kim Hellberg's men and Saints find themselves seventh on 24 points.
  • However, Tonda Eckert's side would be positioned in front of Cesar Peixoto's men were it not for the well-documented four-point deduction imposed on the club relating to Spygate.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Middlesbrough, Wolverhampton Wanderers and Southampton were just three of the clubs earmarked as potential promotion candidates from this season's Championship, and their early-season form proves exactly why that was the case.

Only five points separates all three clubs after 15 games, with Middlesbrough only second on goal difference, whilst Wolves sit two places and just one point behind Kim Hellberg's men and Saints find themselves seventh on 24 points.

However, Tonda Eckert's side would be positioned in front of Cesar Peixoto's men were it not for the well-documented four-point deduction imposed on the club relating to Spygate.

All three head coaches have plenty of difference-makers at their disposal, particularly in attacking areas, with 85 goals scored between their sides so far this campaign.

Wolves and Saints do boast key personnel in this area of the pitch, namely Fer Lopez and Cyle Larin, although both have suffered injury misfortune in recent weeks, but it is fair to say that, after a fresh revelation at the Riverside Stadium, both Peixoto and Eckert will be left feeling extremely frustrated.

Even though Saints confirmed the permanent signing of Larin from RCD Mallorca and Wolves sealed an emotional Molineux return for the at the moment injured Raul Jimenez in the summer, links between the two clubs and various hotshots didn't stop there.

Having excelled on loan at Oxford United last season, there were strong debates over where Will Lankshear's future lay, especially given Tottenham Hotspur's need for further firepower under Roberto De Zerbi.

Off the back of an 11-goal campaign at the Kassam Stadium, Wolves and Southampton became two of many Championship sides linked with a move for the England youth international's signature.

Given Wolves only scored 27 times in last season's Premier League, it was no real surprise when a player with such strong current ability and future potential was identified as a transfer target, but they, like the South Coast side saw offers rejected, albeit figures were never revealed.

Middlesbrough have made great strides of progress since Hellberg's appointment 12 months ago, but one major criticism in the final weeks of last season was the Swede's team's inability to finish off games in which they were the dominant force.

Unsurprisingly, such a trend has continued into this season's early weeks, but after sealing an initial £10m deal with Spurs, which could still rise, Lankshear has certainly solved such a conundrum for the Teesside outfit.

Despite missing Boro's final two games before the international break, which, ironically, Hellberg's side fired blanks in, the 21-year-old's record of 13 goals in as many games matched the feats of ex-Fulham ace, Aleksander Mitrovic, from 2021/22, when the Serbian's 43 goals helped the Cottagers romp to the title under Marco Silva.

As well as his goalscoring exploits, Hellberg recently claimed how impressed he has been with Lankshear's all-round game at such a young age, which has already alerted clubs higher up the pyramid.

Middlesbrough are one of the Championship's best-run clubs at present, having made plenty of cash from the exploits of Djed Spence, Hayden Hackney and Morgan Rogers in recent times.

It seems a matter of when, rather than if Lankshear is the next cab off the rank in this regard, and with the January window looming, exit talk has already begun to surface.

Clubs such as Leeds United and North East rivals, Newcastle United, have recently been credited with interest in the star forward, but in an attempt to retain their prized asset, it has been claimed that Boro have set a remarkable £70m valuation on Lankshear's services.

It has been revealed that middlesbrough fans, what do you make of the valuation placed on Will Lankshear? Comment below!

In July, a five-year deal was agreed between the club and player, and whilst the figure may be eye-watering, it comes as no surprise that Middlesbrough are in no rush to sanction an exit, especially if Lankshear's goals can fire them back to the Premier League, in turn landing greater sums of cash in prize money.

As well as potentially landing his current employers a fortune in terms of transfer fees and the money which comes with promotion, Lankshear is in line to make Tottenham plenty of cash too.

The North London side were unable to agree a 20% sell-on clause with Middlesbrough this summer, but could land at least another £10m in performance-related add-ons, which would be no surprise if the striker's form continues in such a manner.

There is also the chance that, further down the line, Lankshear returns to North London due to a matching rights' clause, which allows Spurs to lodge the exact same sum of cash for his signature should a rival club come in with a bid of their own.

As such, it is certainly a tale of what could have been for both Wolves and Southampton, even if they go on to enjoy their own success this term.

#2471. Breaking: Severe drought and warming increase the extinction risk of cacti

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 29m • 📚 Deep Dive (5785 w)

Breaking: Severe drought and warming increase the extinction risk of cacti

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 29 min read (5785 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~29 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that extreme climatic events are increasing in frequency and intensity with climate change1.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that extreme climatic events are increasing in frequency and intensity with climate change1. Their effects on species’ distributions and extinction risk remain poorly understood2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9. Most species distribution models rely on long-term mean climate, overlooking potentially important nonlinear effects of extremes. Here we integrate upcoming spatial data on severe drought10, including compounding effects of warmer temperatures, with a comprehensive curated dataset of cactus occurrences (648,316 records) and species distribution models to assess how severe drought alters projected suitable climatic area for 993 species of Cactaceae, a highly threatened family11 that is commonly considered drought tolerant. In 91% of cases, models including severe drought were better supported than mean-climate models. Across emissions scenarios (Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSPs) SSP1-2.6 to SSP5-8.5) with 100-km dispersal, including severe drought increased the share of species losing suitable climatic area from 58–61% to 69–72%. The proportion of species projected to lose over a quarter of suitable area increased from 26–43% to 55–58%, and the proportion projected to lose over four-fifths increased from 1–15% to 25–35%. With severe drought, restricting dispersal from 100 to 0 km increased the share losing suitable area from 69–72% to 84–85% across SSPs. These declines reduced regional richness, with five bioregions potentially losing over 25% of species. These findings demonstrate that accounting for climatic extremes can alter assessments of biodiversity vulnerability under climate change. Integrating climatic extremes into ecological forecasting will be critical for assessing biodiversity loss and designing effective conservation strategies across taxa and ecosystems.

Given the data sharing agreement with iNaturalist and private contributors and the widespread risk of illegal collection in Cactaceae, occurrence data used for analyses are available only on request. Requests should be made through correspondence with the corresponding author and, depending on the taxonomic scope of the request, may require an agreement with one or more of the authors (data derived from BIEN or private contributors) or with iNaturalist directly, prohibiting further data sharing. Requests should include a complete list of data consumers and their affiliations, the purpose of the request, the taxonomic scope and a disclosure of any competing interests. Partially obscured iNaturalist data are available72. Average climatic data were retrieved from the CHELSA repository, version 2.1 (https://chelsa-climate.org/). SPEI drought data are available from the NASA Socioeconomic Data and Applications Center (SEDAC; https://www.ciesin.columbia.edu/data/globaldrought/). Soil layers were downloaded from the SoilGrids repository, version 2.0 (https://www.isric.org/explore/soilgrids). Expert distribution maps used to create Extended Data Fig. 7 were obtained from the IUCN Red List of Threatened Species and the IUCN SSC Cactus and Succulent Plants Specialist Group. Bioregion data were downloaded from a previous study52. All Figures and Extended Data Figures are directly reproducible from the Supplementary Information and code at Zenodo123.

All code is available at GitHub (https://github.com/mdpillet/DroughtForecasts) and archived at Zenodo123.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By WILL PICKWORTH, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 17:01 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 17:58 EST, 13 November 2026.

Kevin De Bruyne's wife Michelle has opened up on her family's struggles in Naples and desire to move back home to Belgium one day.

De Bruyne, 35, joined Napoli in the summer of 2025 after leaving Manchester City following a legendary ten-year spell.

But things haven't gone to strategy in Italy, with De Bruyne struggling for fitness in his first season, while he also clashed with former boss Antonio Conte.

The situation hasn't improved much this time around under Max Allegri as Napoli right now sit 10th in Serie A, and reports broke earlier this season that the Belgian midfielder was involved in a dressing room bust-up with team-mates.

And De Bruyne's wife Michele, who he married in 2017, reflected on the turbulence in an interview with Belgian magazine NINA back in September.

It has been revealed that 'Of course, we think about the future together,' he said. 'And increasingly often, we say to each other: "We are going to live here in Limburg. The sooner we get here, the better".'.

Kevin De Bruyne's wife Michelle has opened up on her family's struggles living in Naples.

De Bruyne moved to Napoli in the summer of 2025 after a glittering 10 years at Manchester City.

Limburg is a province in Belgium, and although Michelle insisted that she thought Naples was a beautiful place to live with great weather and food, she spoke about the toll that life in Italy has had on her partner and their three children, Mason, Rome and Suri.

'Kevin leads a very restricted life in Napoli,' she added. 'It's not much fun for him. Besides, we can't do anything together as a family in the city. That's the other side of the coin, isn't it?

It has been revealed that 'In Manchester, it was different. Where we lived, people had seen us so often that it wasn’t special anymore. We could walk out the door there without a single photo being taken. In Naples, that is impossible.'.

She later added: 'At a certain point, football is no longer the priority. You have achieved everything, done everything. Why would you then turn your children’s lives upside down?'.

De Bruyne, who is one of the highest paid players in Italy, signed a two-year contract when he arrived at Napoli but it wasn't certain that he would make it into the second part of that deal in the summer.

Reflecting on his first year ahead of the World Cup, De Bruyne insisted he was 'happy' that Conte had departed.

'Obviously it was difficult for me because Conte has a very different vision of football to mine,' De Bruyne said.

In a recent development, 'In truth, I never had the opportunity to play in my preferred position. In any case, I always tried to give my all for the team. We played very defensively. If you try to win every game by a one-goal margin with a 4-5-1 formation, you play a certain type of football.

De Bruyne signed a two-year deal at Napoli and is unlikely to extend his time in Italy.

'At the start of the season, we sat back even deeper. Our centre-forward scored just 10 goals, so you know the statistics are not going to be great…'.

According to recent reports, he later added: 'For me, yes (I'm happy Conte has gone). As far as I am concerned, he was not obliged to stay. There were promises made last summer on the way that we would be playing, but at the end of the day not much of it happened.

In a recent development, 'I found that a pity. Football needs to be enjoyable, and unfortunately, I found that aspect lacking.

'There’s no point beating around the bush, we have different visions of football. I never got to play in my position under Conte.'.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Will Lanskhear is in the midst of one of the best individual scoring seasons the Championship has ever seen, to the point where there are murmurs of him being tipped to make a move to an elite club as soon as January.

Middlesbrough are reportedly dismissive of those links, which see the 21-year-old admired by the likes of Arsenal and Manchester United, and over the weekend, the Sun stated that Boro had slapped a £70 million price tag on the exciting frontman's head.

Sources indicate that ultimately, that price tag is an indication that Lankshear isn't going anywhere anytime soon, but it won't be long before those links to the traditional 'significant six' sides gain serious legs. The 21-year-old was being suggested for the England squad before injury struck just before the international break.

But he wouldn't be the first young English frontman to make the step to a top club early in his career if he did move on from Middlesbrough in the next 12 months, and he'll have to be wary of being caught up in the expectation that would surround such a move.

It's been a much-discussed question over the past couple of years or so, as Harry Kane entered his 30s, as to who the 'next Harry Kane' would be.

In a recent development, luckily enough, the now all-time record appearance maker for the Three Lions hasn't slowed down; if anything, he's gotten better. But just last summer, that successor looked to be Liam Delap, after he was one of the better performers in Ipswich Town's sole Premier League campaign in 2024/25.

The frontman shone under Liam Rosenior at Hull City during the 2023/24 Championship season, and earned a Premier League move off the back of that with the newly-promoted Tractor Boys.

Ipswich went straight back down, owing mainly to poor defensive numbers. Going forward, Kieran McKenna's side only scored six fewer goals than Everton and eight fewer than Manchester United. Delap was the main source of those, netting 12.

He only netted one brace, too, so he scored in 11 of his 37 league games that year. For his first year at the level in a relegated side, the then-22-year-old was being tipped for significant things, and elite Premier League clubs were interested in him.

After relegation, Delap moved from Ipswich to Chelsea for a £30 million fee.

The Blues fended off interest from Manchester United, Newcastle United and Everton for his signature, and many expected him to net much more than the 12 he did at Portman Road in a side playing in the UEFA Champions League.

Delap contributed to Chelsea winning the Club World Cup in America during the summer of 2025, appearing in every game he was available for and scoring against Esperance.

He was sidelined just three games into the new season with a hamstring injury, though, and upon his return a couple of months later against Wolves in the EFL Cup, he was sent off after receiving two yellow cards in the space of seven minutes.

In a recent development, do you think Liam Delap can still make it to the very top of the English game? Let us know in the comments.

Then-Chelsea boss Enzo Maresca called the sending-off "very stupid" and "embarrassing," and he couldn't really recover after that, even despite his former manager Liam Rosenior coming in after the Italian left in January.

Delap ended the season with one Premier League goal and two in 41 appearances in all competitions. His time at Stamford Bridge was quite a disaster, and he left this past summer. Somehow, Chelsea managed to bank £50 million for his services from Nottingham Forest.

Lankshear already has five more goals in around 1,200 fewer minutes this season than Delap did in his last Championship campaign in 2023/24.

It's evident that he's further along in his development at this stage than his compatriot, but the 21-year-old could look at Delap's trajectory in the past couple of years as an example of what not to do.

Swipe on the pitch or use the pad to move.

In a recent development, joining these big clubs is always a risk, as the amount of pressure on these strikers is massive. It's not just young strikers who fail, either. Look at Viktor Gyokeres, for example; a goalscoring machine at Sporting is now playing back up at Arsenal.

The weight of expectation is even bigger when you're an English striker, too, especially one who has been talked about for a call-up while in the Championship. There'll be a demand for Lankshear to hit the ground running, and if he didn't, he'd be the one being shot at online and amongst pundits.

Honing his craft and not running before he can walk would be wise for Lankshear. It seems as if Middlesbrough are set on keeping him past January, and the likelihood would be that, if they were promoted, he'd do at least one Premier League season at the Riverside, too.

That's not to say that Lankshear should remain out of the spotlight for the next five or so years, however. It's evident that the 21-year-old knows how to handle the mantle of being a line-leader for a side expected to win games at Middlesbrough.

His purpose in Kim Hellberg's side is to get on the end of the many chances that those behind him create, and he's not only gotten into the right positions consistently, but he's finished opportunities exceptionally.

Lankshear could probably make the jump to a Premier League side in the next year or so, but at Middlesbrough, he's in a position where he can afford to gain more and more confidence as the focal point of a good team, with there still plenty of time for him to make that step-up.

If he does go to an Arsenal or a Manchester United in the future, doing so as a 23-year-old with a hundred-odd appearances for Middlesbrough, some of which coming in the Premier League, would suit him much better in the long term.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Recent findings suggest that ronaldo has found himself at the centre of a growing dispute after abruptly leaving Portugal’s national team camp following a reported disagreement with head coach Jorge Jesus.
  • Jamie Carragher, however, believes Ronaldo’s reputation should not shield him from criticism when his behaviour becomes difficult to defend.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Jamie Carragher has taken aim at Rio Ferdinand for defending Cristiano Ronaldo following the Portuguese forward’s latest controversy with his national team.

Recent findings suggest that ronaldo has found himself at the centre of a growing dispute after abruptly leaving Portugal’s national team camp following a reported disagreement with head coach Jorge Jesus. The incident has prompted strong reactions from former teammates and pundits, with Ferdinand firmly siding with the Al-Nassr star.

Jamie Carragher, however, believes Ronaldo’s reputation should not shield him from criticism when his behaviour becomes difficult to defend.

Rio Ferdinand, who played alongside Cristiano Ronaldo at Manchester United between 2003 and 2009, criticised Jorge Jesus for the way he handled the situation.

Speaking on his Rio Presents podcast, the former United captain criticised Jesus for not showing respect to Cristiano Ronaldo.

According to recent reports, “Cristiano Ronaldo was put in a very bad situation and was treated in an inappropriate way. He has an enormous history in football. Jorge Jesus did not deal with Ronaldo well and chose to treat him in that way, but I cannot find any explanation for it,” Ferdinand said.

In a recent development, despite Jesus being Portugal’s manager, Ferdinand questioned his standing, comparing him with the likes of Sir Alex Ferguson and Pep Guardiola. To say the least, Ferdinand only embarrassed himself doing that.

Jamie Carragher saw the argument very differently and rightfully so.

Speaking on The Overlap Daily, the former Liverpool defender suggested that Ferdinand’s friendship with Ronaldo was influencing his reaction to the incident.

“People think it’s good to be close to people in the game, but this is where it becomes a problem,” Carragher explained.

He then called out both Ferdinand and broadcaster Piers Morgan, who has also been vocal in his support of Ronaldo.

“People like Piers Morgan and Rio Ferdinand, who are big people in the media whether you like them or not, are embarrassing themselves with the nonsense that they’re coming out with because they know Ronaldo. You can know someone and try to look after them, but you cannot defend the indefensible.”.

Carragher believes Ronaldo’s achievements should not put the forward beyond criticism, particularly when his actions involve his national team and its management.

Gary Neville, who also played with Cristiano Ronaldo, has questioned Ronaldo’s handling of the situation, despite his longstanding affection for his former Manchester United teammate.

Neville argued that Ronaldo’s public response had made matters worse and the forward needed to accept criticism rather than expect others to defend him.

It has been revealed that “With Cristiano, it’s difficult because I love him, but I can’t watch what happened at United in his second period and then see him make a statement like that without saying something. He has to be pulled up on that and told that it isn’t acceptable,” Neville remarked.

He also suggested Ronaldo’s extraordinary success, wealth and influence could have contributed to a sense that he was beyond challenge.

“When you have a billion pounds in the bank, the achievements he has had and the power he has, you feel you’re unbreakable, you feel you’re unstoppable,” Neville added.

Despite his criticism, Neville does not believe the episode will define Ronaldo’s legacy permanently. He expects the attention to fade once the forward retires, allowing his achievements on the pitch to take centre stage again.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Birmingham City's season has got off to a flyer, and now plenty of discourse throughout the November international break has revolved around how Chris Davies could further strengthen his squad in the January transfer window.

Blues' recent form sees them top the Championship on goal difference ahead of Middlesbrough and Stoke City, and they return to action this weekend to take on the latter at the Bet365 Stadium.

Not many outside the walls of St. Andrew's @ Knighthead Park envisaged such a remarkable start, but supporters in this part of the world are now dreaming of a first Premier League season since 2011.

As well as looking assured in defence, Davies' tactical reshuffles in recent months have made Birmingham a real threat in their attacking play, particularly on the counter-attack through the speed and direct nature of Liam Millar, Patrick Roberts, Jay Stansfield and August Priske.

Millar's predicament, in particular, has been a hot topic of debate in recent weeks given the nature of his loan move from Premier League newcomers, Hull City.

The Canadian international's impact in B9 has slightly decreased in recent weeks compared to his flying start, but Football League World's Birmingham City fan pundit, Jason Moore, has issued the sum of cash Blues should look to front up for his services.

Millar, 27, signed for Hull on a three-year contract from FC Basel in August 2024, making just 53 appearances at the MKM Stadium in the process due to a serious injury.

The 48-time international was a regular in Sergej Jakirovic's play-off winning team last season, but was loaned out to Birmingham in September despite scoring what could be a crucial winner for the Tigers against Coventry City on August 29th.

He has since registered four goals and three assists in 11 games for Blues, and when asked how much money the club should pay for a permanent transfer, Moore told FLW: "His current form, where he's contract-wise and the relationship he seems to have at Hull, I think £5m is fair for all parties involved.

"He started really well for us, but he's not banging in loads and loads of goals. I know that sounds harsh because he has had a very good start and he does look a threat. But I just think £5m is fair," he added.

Sources indicate that "Hull get a decent value, his contract's running out. I know they have the extension on him, but I do think it's a fair price all-round, to be fair. It depends on how much more they want.

According to recent reports, "If they want £7m, I'd be looking at an add-ons deal potentially. But, I think £5-7m is more than fair. Anything else, you start to get a little bit silly.

Industry observers note that "It all depends on where we are as well come January. If we're making a real push to get promoted, then do you want to put that money elsewhere because we've got Millar and then revisit in the summer?

"I think it depends on where we are and what the asking price is. But, right now, I think £5-7m is probably fair.".

In September, Birmingham fended off competition from both Middlesbrough and Stoke for Millar's services, and it is a deal which has certainly paid off thus far.

Davies has two experienced options to select from on the left flank, with Demarai Gray also scoring three times this season after previous injury concerns.

However, it is clear how much attention to detail went into making the deal possible, with the Blues boss revealing after the loan was confirmed: "I've tried to get him in a few transfer windows now - but never been able to.

According to recent reports, "He's a player with a lot of experience of this league. We've had to be patient and finally we've got him. And the fact that he's coming to us indicates a lot, as he had a lot of options.".

With Hull now in the Premier League, the market valuations of many players at the MKM Stadium have increased, and Millar was no exception to that rule, with it being claimed his current value sits at £4.1m.

Sources indicate that that, of course, could increase again if his output at St. Andrew's continues to be strong between now and May in Birmingham's own promotion push.

Blues fans, how much money should Knighthead pay to sign Liam Millar permanently? Comment below!

Hull supporters were recently left perplexed by the Canadian's admissions in a post-match interview, with some even debating that he would never play for the club again.

However, the Tigers still have plenty to say when it comes to his future, as if they extend his contract until 2028, Blues would certainly be forced to cough up a greater sum of cash for his services.
